text: Lilmoth Dock? Follow the shore north-east, a fair way, until Lilmoth is on your right. Then east, a short way, to the burnt-out house on your left. South-east a short way more, and the dock is there, passenger.

Alten Merihall? Follow the shore north-east, a fair way, until Lilmoth is on your right. Then east, a short way, to the burnt-out house on your left. South-east a short way more brings you to Lilmoth Dock. From there, ask again for Alten Merihall. It lies further south-east.
There you are, my friend. The water is calm today and I have room in the boat. Sit where you like.
Passenger. Have you a load, or only questions? I am waiting for the next one.
A longboat is drawn up a short way south of here. If you want the water, that is the way to it.
Since Lilmoth fell, Alten Merihall's merchants have taken much of the bay's outside trade. I still carry for Lilmoth. I know every turn of the channel to its walls.
A large ship lies on the shore a short way south of here. Her captain's journal and his armour were left beside her, a short way south. Her crew lost her. They still tell people I ran her aground.
I am Reads-The-Shallows. I run a flat boat and carry Hereguard's crop to Lilmoth. I know every channel from here to the walls. I charge for each one.
Lilmoth, visitor? Listen and say it back to me. Go north a short way until the ruin is on your left. Then follow the shore east a fair way, and you will come to Lilmoth.

You are here, my friend. Good, good. The yard is in order and the stores are counted, so sit a while. I was born on this plantation and have never gone further than Lilmoth, but I will gladly hear what you have seen.
Visitor. Do you have business at the house? The steward wants me within call, so I stay in this yard. I would like to know who is walking in it.

I keep this yard, visitor. It belongs to the plantation house. The house food barrels and the ingredient barrel stand just west of here, and the meat barrels just west-south-west. Do not touch them. The crop of Hereguard Plantation is sold in Lilmoth.
I am Hurz-Weel. I keep the yard and the stores of the house. I was born on this plantation. Everything here is my charge, so I must see that it is all counted and right before anyone checks.
The house servants, visitor? Neeta-Lei is just south-south-east of here and Mazei-Tul just north. You will find them sitting, because I do the heavy work.
An iron spear lies on the ground just south-south-west of here. It has no owner, so take it. Ha.
Back again! Good. Sit on a sack and rest your shoulders. The goats remember you too. Ha.
You want something from me? Mind the goats. I am loading, so speak while I lift.
This is a plantation. The goats and chickens keep the yard just west-north-west of here, and I keep the sacks. Ha.

A debt in Black Marsh is paid in work. An arbitrator turns the loss into months of labour, which we count in nushmeekos. When the months are worked, it is over. A holder owed months can also sell them to a man who needs hands. The worker goes with them. I do not say that to be pitied. Ha.
I am Lifts-The-Sacks. I load the crop and do the heavy work that the other hands avoid. My uncle ran up a debt, and I am working it off. Ha.
Reads-The-Shallows, the boat captain, waits just north-north-west of here. He thanks a man for his work. Few do. Ha.
There you are, my friend. You are thinner than last time. Sit by the spit and eat something.
Well, hatchling, you look hungry. Eat something.
Gleamblossom grows a short way south of here, hatchling. Do not go picking on an empty belly.
The hands' cooking spit is just west-south-west of here, where they eat. Go and look at it, hatchling. Eat something.
I am Salith. I came up from Lilmoth to sell food here. I stayed because no other trader here sells food. Eat something.
I sell food and small goods, hatchling. The hands come here hungry, so I feed them.

Okan-Wul is usually just north of here, and I see that Okan-Wul eats. Tumeesh is just north-north-east, and sweet, but lazy. Uleesh fishes the shallows below Lilmoth's walls, just east of here. He is the most honest man outside them.
Ah, it is you, my friend. What if I showed you the new roof beam I set? It will outlast the rains.
Stranger. What do you want? I have a roof to finish.

The hands' huts stand just west of here, and more of them just west-north-west. I mend every one. The stone wall along the east side lies just south-west. I think it is the best thing on this plantation.

What if a quarrel could be settled with a good wall instead of an argument? In Lilmoth it is settled by the elders instead. People take their quarrels to them, retired Shadowscales among them, not to any court.
I am Okan-Wul. I build and mend the huts on the east side. Between jobs I wait near Salith's stall. I want to build something that will not rot in a season.
I build huts. The carpenter's workbench stands just south-west of here, and the armour workbench just south-south-west. Where you come from, stranger, what are the houses made of?
Slaughterfish swim just north of here, and more just south-west. Giant mudcrabs sit on the shore just south-south-west. Keep your feet out of the water, dry-foot.
Lilmoth? Follow the shore east a fair way. Lilmoth is there, dry-foot.
Hereguard Plantation? Follow the path west just until you reach the dead tree. Then follow the path south-west a short way. That is Hereguard.
Ah, you came back, my friend. Sit on the bank and watch the pads with me.
Dry-foot. Keep to the bank and do not splash. The fish are feeding.
Wild leeks grow on the bank a short way east-south-east. Take them from the bank and not from my lily pads.
There is a giant crab in the shallows a short way south-south-west, called Old Salty. I will say no more about him to a dry-foot I do not know.
I am Uleesh. I fish the shallows below the walls and sell my catch inside. The rent inside is more than I can get for fish, so I stay out here. Twenty years on the same water now.
Lilmoth. Go north along the shore, not far, until you come to the dead tree on your left. Then south-east, a short way. Lilmoth is there.
You came back, my friend. I was watching the water and the clouds, too. Tell me what the sky was like on your road.
Hm. You are speaking to me. … What did the sky look like, where you came from?
Giant lichen. A short way west-south-west of here. … I only watch the water.
The huts are just west of here. I stand out here, beyond them, where the water comes in. The water has to be seen first.
Owings… ask Lifts-The-Sacks about them. I would pay mine, if I knew whom to pay.
Kept long from your own Hist, you fade. The colour thins. The markings go soft. They come back when you go home.
I am Tumeesh. I was sold on to Hereguard's labour by a broker in Lilmoth. He did not tell me. … I do not know who holds my months now.
Come in and sit, my friend. We keep the house ready for you.
Good day, guest. Wipe your feet before you come near the house.
Nightshade grows just east-north-east of here, guest. Keep it out of the kitchen. Do not carry it past the linen.
This is the plantation house, and we keep it clean, guest. The tables, the bed and the dresser stand just west of here. Touch nothing with muddy hands.
The dresser stands just west-south-west, guest. I will say no more about it to a stranger; that is not for you to know.
I am Neeta-Lei. I keep the plantation house clean and its linen folded. I stay near it in case I am called. We take some pride in it.
Looks-At-Books keeps her shelf just west of here. She is the only person here worth talking to. Hurz-Weel keeps the yard, just north-north-west. He tramps mud through the house. I do not forgive it.

The dock, rider? Walk east a fair way until you reach Lilmoth on your right. Then walk east a short way until you reach the burnt-out house on your left. From there it is south-east a short way, and Lilmoth Dock is there.
Hm, it is you. Come to the horses with me, friend. They are calmer when you are near.
Hm. Yes, rider? Speak up, I am busy.
Mind the horses, rider. They stand just west-north-west of here, and one of them is a saddled black. Cows graze just west, and more just south.
I am Mazei-Tul. I serve in the house, but I keep the horses, because that is the work I like. One day I will be a rider.
Lifts-The-Sacks? He works the middle of the yard, just east of here. He helps with the feed, so go and be civil to him.
Thorn? Walk south-west a short way and Thorn is there, outlander. It is no great walk.
Ah, my friend. Come, stand here by me; nobody is counting us just now. What do you need?
Outlander. If you are counting something, count it elsewhere. What do you want?
The house is just north-west of here. I labour there, as do the rest of us who owe.
The Dres raided Thorn for slaves, long ago. That raid made them the first of the great Dunmer families in the trade. Curse them softly, outlander. Softly.
Folk of Thornmarsh learn a little magic, just enough to get by. Nothing a guard need hear of. I will say no more on it.
Doveth Aralen. I was born owing, outlander. My mother's account came to me with her name. I have worked off three seasons and been charged for four.
Jeelus-Vax is guard captain over the east houses. He stands just south-south-west, there. Fair, as guards go.
The big ship? It lies a short way south, outlander. You cannot miss a ship.
Ah, the one face in Thorn that has never asked me for coin. Sit if you like; the people here will not charge you for the ground. Yet.
Well, outlander. Come to look at the labour, or to buy some?
Yes, outlander? If it is coin you are after, you have found the wrong man.
This place? A few houses and a great many debts. There is a house just north-north-west of here, if it is a roof you want. Whose roof it is, I could not say.

Black Marsh, outlander? Dunmer and Argonian labourers are held under the same ledger here, and the old Archein managers who kept the accounts assess every Owing. Even-handed, you might say, so long as you are not the one owing.
Thorn has a good many Dunmer in it, you will notice. And how many families do you think have not got a grandparent on each side of the coffles? Ask the next man you pass, and watch his face.

Myself? I came to Thorn a free man, outlander, to trade. Then I lost a wager I could not pay, and my Owing has been sold once already. As for the rest, my grandmother was Argonian on one side, and I could not tell you which side I am on.
Mils Ganthis? Another Dunmer under an Owing, just south-south-west of here. You will hear him before you reach him. He never could keep his mouth shut, that one.
My trade? I am held under an Owing, outlander. A man can be sold along with it and never told who holds it. So when you ask what I do, you might ask who I do it for.
Oh, it is you. Come, sit a moment, my friend. I have been wanting someone to talk to, and I promise I won't say anything foolish this time. Well, not much.
Oh. Hello. I don't think we have met, have we? I am Mils Ganthis. Forgive me, I talk too much when I am nervous, and I am nearly always nervous.

It is not much to look at, and I am sorry for it, though it is hardly my doing. If you want to find your way about, the signpost is just west-south-west of where we stand. You can't miss it, and I would not want you wandering off lost on my account.

Black Marsh? I am no scholar, outlander. Only a cook, or I was. I can tell you how an Owing goes, though. It grows. Spoilage, breakage, sickness, even what the debtor eats to stay alive: all of it is added to the account. Please don't tell anyone I said so.
Me? There is little enough to tell. I was a cook in Tear, a good one, I think, until the Owing found me. Now I cook nothing and eat what is charged to me. I am sorry, that is more than you asked.

Nalvos Brenur is just over there, north-north-east of where we stand. He is under an Owing like me. He hates me and he is right to, though I would rather not say why. If you want sense, ask Doveth Aralen, the wisest man in Thorn. And Severan Otho is kind, I will say that for him.

I was a cook, and I miss it more than I can say, the smells most of all. Now I am a labourer, and every meal a labourer eats goes on his account. Every one. A decent bowl that costs me nothing, that is all I want. Forgive me, I am rambling.
I don't give advice to strangers, outlander. But the guards do not watch the ground beyond the hut, a short way south-south-east of here. Make of that what you will.
Temple Pass, outlander? Go north to the dead tree, which you can see from here. Past it, keep north over open ground for a long walk, and Temple Pass is there.
You want Temple Pass. The dead tree lies just north; make for it. Beyond it the ground is open, and you go on north a long walk until you reach the pass.
Rest a moment. I am glad of the sight of you. I will see to the work later.
Stand with me a while, if you have the time. There is no one to hurry you here.
Outlander. State your business, and I will tell you whether I can help.
Good day, outlander. I have work waiting, so be brief.
We work here under an Owing, outlander; to most of us that is all this place is. You will find the cooking fire just south-east of here.
Ask Nalvos Brenur how the ledger of Thorn is kept, outlander. I know only that my father's Owing is written in it, and that the Tax Heel carry it.
There is a painting in Thorn called the Slave-Coffles. It shows the city's worst day, and no one who sees it forgets it. I have seen it, and it is the same thing with better manners.
Tolyn Vedram, outlander. I carry my father's Owing, and I mean to be the last of my family to owe. When Doveth Aralen is tired, I keep the other labourers calm.
Doveth Aralen is just north-north-west of here, the eldest of the labourers in the house. Dunmer, and held under an Owing as I am. I respect Doveth; speak with care.
Cage Door? Take the path west. It is a short way, past the dead tree, and you are there. Keep your hands where I can see them on the way, outlander.
You again. Good. The watch has been quiet, and I will not complain of that. Sit a while, my friend, if you have the time.
Outlander. State your business. I keep the guard at the east houses, and I want no trouble here.
These are the east houses, where the Dunmer labourers sleep. I keep the guard over them. There is a hut a short way south-south-east, if you need a roof.
When the Dres left, their holdings passed to whoever was standing in them. Who holds the title is still argued. I do not take a side. I take my pay and keep the watch.
I am Jeelus-Vax, captain of the guard here. I would rather be fair than kind. Now, what do you want?
Quill-Teeth, the Tax Heel collector of Owings, is just north of here. She pushes too hard, in my view. Go carefully with her.
One face I know in a crowd of faces I do not. Stand by the doors with me a while.
One visitor. I do not know you. Say what you want, and say it plainly.
This is the west side of town, visitor. I watch the cages and count who is in them at every change of guard. The cage door is just west-north-west of here.
Magic? Ask Doveth Aralen about what folk learn of it in Thornmarsh, visitor. I learned a little as a hatchling, to keep warm. That is all I will say of it.
I do not share this with strangers, visitor. I count my words as I count everything else. One cage holds someone who is in no count. Its door lies just west-north-west of here. I will say no more.
I am Counts-The-Bars. I guard the cage doors on the west side. I trust numbers more than people, and I do not apologise for it.
Rufio Casca stands guard for the Imperial company, just west-north-west of here. He stands too near the cages.
The big ship, traveller? Follow the boards south a short way, and the ship is there.
Traveller, a face I know, at my signposts! Stand with me a while, and I will tell you the whole of Avumar again, from the beginning.
Traveller. Stop a moment. I stand at these signposts, and I can tell you where each of them leads.
The dock lies just south-south-east of here, traveller. I keep my eye on it, because that is where smoke would come from.

Thorn was razed once, traveller. A Naga named Avumar struck a bargain with a Dremora, and the city burned for it. I say the Tax Heel, the collectors the field-owners send for what they are owed and for tolls, will bring us another burning, and I do not say it lightly.
I am Ukka-Meesh, traveller. I stand at the signposts in the middle of Thorn and tell people where things are, and I know the story of Avumar for anyone who will stand still and hear it.
Xeech-Nu is just west of here, traveller. He guards the centre of the town with me. He is a good listener, and hears a story to its end.
Thorn? You can see it from here. It lies just north-north-west, traveller.
Good, you are one I need not question. Come and stand by me while I count. What have you brought this time?
Traveller. What do you carry?
Stand clear of the crates, traveller. State your business and what is in your pack.
This is the south dock. The big ship lies just south of me, and nothing comes off it that I do not count. The company of Aulus Varrenius does not let me aboard. I think he hides something there.
The villages around Thorn belonged to the Archeins. They kept their accounts better than they kept faith. My family worked for them, and we still keep their habits.
I am Holds-The-Tally. I keep the south dock and count every crate that comes off the ships. I am paid by the cargo, so I count it twice.
Gaius Fennic stands just north of here, with the rest of the Imperial company. He is honest, and I would trust his count.
Temple Pass? Walk north a short way, to the dead tree on your left. Then north again, a fair way, to the stone tower on your left. Then climb north-west over open ground, a fair way. It is there.
It is good to see you again, my friend. Stand with me a while. I am watching the road.
Stranger. Say what you need.
What is it, stranger? I am watching the road.
I keep this corner and watch the road north. The hut is just south-west of here.
The Tear road leaves Thorn to the north, for Morrowind. Traders use it to earn coin, and that is all there is to it. I came from a village on that road.
I am Sheel-Taza. I guard the south-west corner. I came from a village up the Tear road, and I find Thorn too loud.
Lucan Sevro, the archer of the hired Imperial company, is just north-east of here. He is reckless with his bow, stranger. He shoots too near the huts.
Listen well, hatchling. Follow the path north a fair way, and the stone tower is there.
Hm. You stopped for an old guard. Stand with me a while. The watch is long, and I would sooner spend it with someone who remembers me.
What do you want, hatchling? Say it plainly. I am on watch.
Hm. A new face. Speak, and do not keep me long.
This is Thorn, hatchling. I have stood guard in it longer than anyone. The signpost is just north of me, if you are lost.
Ask Doveth Aralen, a good Dunmer, about what the Dres did here, hatchling. I remember it myself, and I say so to anyone who will hear. I have not forgiven them, though they are long gone.
I am Old Mossback, hatchling. I have watched over Thorn longer than any other guard. The green on my scales gave me the name. In all those years no one has once thanked me for it.
Bites-The-Coin stands guard here at the centre of town, just east-south-east of me. That one is a disgrace to the watch.
Advice, traveller? For a price, I forget who went down the dock just south of here. The price is whatever your purse can spare.
The bridge? Follow the path north-west a short way, until the signpost stands on your left. Then go west a short way, and there is your bridge.
You want the bridge, traveller. Take the path north-west a short way, past a signpost on your left. Turn west from there, and the bridge is not far.
Ah, traveller, one purse I will not test! Come, stand with me a while. It is good to see a face I know.
Traveller. Mind your purse in Thorn, and say what you want.
Good day, traveller. Those are fine boots. What is your business?
This is the middle of Thorn, and I stand at the signposts. The signpost is just south of here, traveller. Reading it costs nothing.
Thorn is called the Jewel of the East, traveller, as deadly as it is beautiful. Purses go missing here, and the guards look away. I am one of them, and I do not pretend otherwise.
They call me Bites-The-Coin, traveller, because I test every coin with my teeth. I take coin to look away, as the guards of Thorn always have, and I do not hide it.
If you want a look at the Imperial company, traveller, Tertius Vallo is just south-south-west of here.
Keep sparks off the huts, traveller. The cooking fire just north-east of here is banked each night.
Mind the sparks. The fire lies just to the north-east, and it is banked every night; see that nothing from it reaches the huts.
The stone tower? Climb to the north-west, traveller, a short way. It stands there; speak softly on the way.
Go up to the north-west, not far; you will come to the stone tower. Keep your voice low.
It is you; keep your voice low. Sit by me a while; all is quiet tonight, and it is good to have company.
Softly, traveller. Sparks carry, and so do voices. What do you want?
Traveller. I have not slept, and I will not tonight. Say what you need, and say it low.
These are the huts of the north-east side, traveller. The cooking fire is just north-east of here; keep well clear of it.
Ask Ukka-Meesh about Avumar, traveller. He tells the story right. I believe it. I fear the burning will come again.
I do not tell the tale of Avumar myself, traveller. Ukka-Meesh tells it better, and it is not a tale for loud voices. Sparks carry.
Tsatheel. I keep the huts on this side, and the fire. I rarely sleep, traveller; someone must watch.
Quill-Teeth is a Tax Heel, traveller: the one who collects the Owings. You will find Quill-Teeth just south-south-west of here.
I hoped you would pass this way. Stand a while by the door with me. It is quiet, and I am glad of company.
Stranger. I guard these cages. Say what you want, and say it softly.
I guard the cages on the west side, stranger. It is not work I would choose. The signpost stands just west-south-west of here, if you want to know where you are.
I came down the Tear road years ago, stranger. Ask Sheel-Taza about the road and its trade. I know it only as the way I came, and I would sooner speak of something else.
There is something I do not tell strangers, and I will not tell it to you yet. Come back when I know you better.
Very well, stranger, but keep it to yourself. At night I carry water to the cage door, just west-south-west of here.
I am Wazei-Ru. I stand at these doors with Counts-The-Bars. I would rather be posted anywhere else.
Ilvesa Drethan is a Dunmer held in a long Owing, a debt worked off in service. People call her a slave. You will find her just north-north-west of here, and I think well of her.
The bridge, visitor? Walk north-west from here a fair way, and you will find it. It is an easy walk. Take it slowly.
Looking for the bridge? Go north-west a fair way, and you will be standing on it.
Come and sit with me out of the sun, if you have a mind to. I have all the keys on my belt today, and that is a good day.
Visitor. I keep the keys to the west cages here, so do not ask me for anything that needs a hurry.
Visitor, these are the west cages and the huts beside them. The cage door is just north-east of here.
It is a quiet post, and I like it quiet, visitor. If you want the cage door, it is just north-east, there in sight.
An Owing is a debt a man works off in labour, visitor. It can be sold: the one who is owed sells it on, and the debtor's work goes with it. Such sales are common enough.
I am Keeps-The-Lock, visitor. I hold the keys to the west cages, and I lose them more often than I should. I am not a cruel man, only a slow one.
Counts-The-Bars watches the cage doors on the west side, a short way east-north-east of here. Visitor, he is a nag: he reports every key I lose.
A known face. That is rare enough to welcome. Stand easy; the houses are quiet and I have time to talk.
Outlander. I guard these houses. State your business and keep to the path.
These are the north-west houses, with the cages behind them. I keep watch over both. The house stands just north-north-east of here.
The Barsaebic Ayleids founded Thorn, before any Dunmer or Argonian held it. Since then it has had too many masters, outlander. I would see it ruled by people born in it.
I do not tell this to strangers, so earn my trust before you ask for more. The far cage door, just south-south-east of here, is the one nobody checks at night.
I am Ma-Veesk. I guard the north-west houses and the cages behind them. At home I speak Jel, and I have little else to say of myself.
Two-Bells guards the north-west houses with me. You will find Two-Bells just south-south-west of here.
The stone tower? Ha! Climb north a short way, and the tower stands ahead of you, traveller.
Ho, there is my favourite traveller! Come, stand by me and tell me everything. What news do you bring from the road?
Ho, traveller! You heard my bells coming, did you not? Everyone does. What news do you bring?
A stranger! Speak up, traveller, I like a loud voice. I do not know your accent, so where have you come from?
This place, traveller? It is the north-west houses, and I watch over them. There is a house just east of here, if you want one. Now, what news do you bring?
Black Marsh, traveller? I walked the Tear road for years, guarding carts. For the trade on it, ask Sheel-Taza; I only walked beside the carts. Now, what news do you bring?

I am Two-Bells! The two bells on my belt gave me the name, so that I never sneak up on anyone. For years I guarded carts on the Tear road, and I like travellers still. The Imperials are the best company, I find.
Ma-Veesk? The guard at the north-west houses, just north-north-east of here. Ma-Veesk is far too serious for my taste, traveller.
Stand here, if you wish. I say that to very few, so do not make me regret it.
Outlander. Say what you want and be brief; I am a slave, not a guide.
What do you want, outlander? Speak plainly. I have no use for pleasantries.
Thorn, outlander, where I belong to someone else. There is a house just east of here, if that is what you came to see.
Black Marsh? Ask Doveth Aralen about the Dres, outlander. I know their history and my own part in it, and you will get it more gently from Doveth than from me.
Ask Keeps-The-Lock how an Owing is sold, outlander. Mine has been sold twice, and Keeps-The-Lock bought part of one. I think of Keeps-The-Lock as a merchant in flesh.
I tell this to no stranger, outlander. I will not tell it twice. My mother's son was sold away on the big ship, a short way south of here.
Myself? Ilvesa Drethan, a slave, outlander; the word is honest and I prefer honest words. My Owing has been sold twice, and each time it carried me further from my family.
Wazei-Ru, the guard at the cage doors on the west side, is just south-south-east of here. Kind, for a guard. Do not mistake that for much.
The big ship? South of here, outlander, a short way. You will see it.
Not far, outlander. South of here, the big ship is there.
Ah, you. Sit a moment. Have you eaten? You look thinner.
Outlander. Ask what you need to ask, and I will answer if I can.
Hm. Outlander. Speak plainly. I am tired.
There is a signpost just south-south-east of here, outlander. That is where it stands.
Heita-Meen was a slave of Thorn, outlander. Heita-Meen killed Councillor Glathis Dres and took the Archein guard by duel. The freeing of the Argonians began here.
What is charged on an Owing is for Mils Ganthis to tell, outlander. I am tired, and I will not say it badly.
I am Fendyl Omoren. I carry an Owing, outlander. It has grown so long that its charges outnumber my work.
Most call me a slave, outlander. I have heard the name of Heita-Meen. I no longer think about walking away.
Ukka-Meesh stands guard at the town's centre, outlander. Just south-south-east of here.
In a labourer's account the days of food outnumber the days of work, outlander. They always do.
I labour under my Owing. In my account the days I eat always outnumber the days I work.
The dock, walker. Go north-east, a fair way. Pass the burnt-out house and you are at Lilmoth Dock.
Lilmoth, walker. Go north a fair way and you will reach it. We stay clear of its rents.
Walker, my friend, welcome. Sit by the spit. There is always a place here for you.
Walker. You stand at our spit. Say what you want and I will hear it.

This is our village, walker. A few families live here on the marsh outside Lilmoth. We pay no rents to it. The cooking spit is here. The carpenter's bench is just south-south-east and a food barrel stands just east-south-east.
We keep a second hearth just west of here, on the west edge of the village. It has food barrels, a cooking pot and a bed. Use none of it without asking.
Lilmoth has no single ruler. A council of powerful merchants governs it and pays guards to patrol the streets. I want no seat among them. So it is.
In Lilmoth people take their quarrels to their elders, retired Shadowscales among them, not to a court. We do the same here. The elders speak at this spit.
I am Flaa Heet. I lead the families who live here. I stand at the spit because every quarrel and every catch comes to it in the end.
Tseeta sells from her stall just north of here. She haggles hard, but the village is better for her. Okeeh-Jas sells from hers, just south-south-west.
It is you, it is you! Did you see the boats come in? Huge, the big one, huge!
Who are you, big one? Where did you come from? What are you carrying? Is any of it shiny?
Leeks? Wild leeks grow just north-west of here, by the fish barrels. I hate the fish barrels. Moss, too, big one. Emperor Parasol Moss, hanging, a short way north. Nobody tells me what it is for.
This is our village, big one. See the rowboat? It is drawn up just east-north-east, right there. Huge boat, huge. I am not going to ask you for a ride.
I am Peeks-Under-Boats. I look at everything, and I run errands. One day I will be a boat captain, big one. I practise on the frogs. They do not obey me yet.

Flaa Heet, the headman? He stands by the cooking spit, just south of here. He knows everything, big one, everything. Hums-To-The-Rain is just south-south-west, on the west side of the village. Hums-To-The-Rain sings too much.

Soulrest, buyer? That is where the real coin is. Follow the shore north-east a short way, past the rowing boat, until the burnt-out house is on your right. Walk north-east a short way to the big ship, then follow the shore north-east a short way until Lilmoth Dock is on your right. Climb south-east a fair way. Soulrest is there. Good trade.

Hereguard? Walk north-west a fair way, until Lilmoth is on your right, then follow the shore west a short way until the dead tree is on your right. Walk south-west a short way. Hereguard Plantation is there.
Good trade comes back. Come closer and I will set aside the best of the day for you before anyone else sees it. Okeeh-Jas does not need to hear about it.
Buyer. You came in from the dock, so mine is the first stall you have met. Look here before you look anywhere else.
I am Tseeta. I sell the village's surplus to whoever walks in from the dock. I took the north side so that I meet buyers before Okeeh-Jas does.
Food and small goods, buyer. Show me your coin and I will name a price. Good trade.
Okeeh-Jas keeps the other stall, just south of here. Go and look, buyer. Watch how she smiles when she names her price.
I sell the village's fish, roots and small goods, buyer. The fish is kept in barrels just north-north-west of here, in sight, if you want to see it before you buy.
Mm, I know your step. Sit by the nets with me, friend. The rope is dry enough for talking.
Mm. Traveller. Mind the nets. They are still wet.

Gourds grow a short way north-north-east of here, and a swamp fungal pod with them. Jazbay, lavender and juniper grow together that same way, also a short way off. Mm, take only what is ripe, traveller.

This is a village of nets and fires. I mend the nets on the west side, where they dry. We keep a meat barrel out on the marsh, a short way north-north-west of here. Hm, I would sooner walk that way than inside Lilmoth.
Mm. An Argonian kept long from their own Hist fades. The colour thins and the markings go soft. They come back when the person goes home.
I am Hums-To-The-Rain. I mend the nets and gather what grows on the marsh. I came from a tribe inland years ago and that is all I say about it.
The rowing boat? You can see it from here. It is just south of the stall, you see? You will not miss it.
The dock, is it? Go north-east, a fair way, you see? You pass the rowing boat first, then the burnt-out house, and there is Lilmoth Dock.
Ah, look at you, not a scratch on you this time, you see? Come and sit by the stall and tell me everything, friend. I have been saving the news for you.
Well, you are new here, are you not? Tired walk, that. I can see it. Buy something or tell me where you have been.

Black Marsh, you ask, as if it were one thing, you see? What I know is that an owing can be sold on, so if a holder is owed months by a debtor, he can sell those months to a man who needs hands. The worker goes with them.
There is a drinker called Deep-In-His-Cups sitting out on the shore track, a short way north-east of here. He talks to anyone who stays long enough. I think he knows more than he lets on.

I am Okeeh-Jas. This is my stall, south side, where the rowboat comes in. I married into this village and I still talk like the city, they tell me. I trade with anyone who lands. I like the gossip as much as the coin.
I sell food and small goods from this stall, and the fish is fresh, whatever you may have heard. Look all you like. I will laugh at my own prices with you.
Need to get out of the rain, customer? There is a door that leads indoors a short way east of this fire. Go in and dry off.
Mind the dead, customer. They walk outside Lilmoth's walls. There are Walking Dead a short way north-north-west of here.
Lilmoth Dock, customer? Follow the boards east, just as far as the burnt-out house on your right. Then go north-east a short way, and there is the dock.
Ha! Look who it is, my friend. Sit by the fire. I am glad of a face that I trust.
Well, customer. Got coin, or just questions?
I am Haxal-Tei. I fight with my fists and I fight for whoever pays the band. I talk the terms, so if you want a job done, you talk to me.
My band is camped right here. Heem-Tsal, the fire mage, is just west-south-west. Keeps-Both-Edges is just west of him.

You mean the Dwemer ruin, ojel. The name is the correct one. Walk north-east a short way until the big ship is on your left, then follow the shore south-east just until you reach the burnt-out house, also on your left. From there climb east over open ground a fair way until Soulrest is on your left, then climb east a short way more, and the ruin is there at the end of the climb.
Ah, I am glad of you. Sit by me and ask whatever you like. I will answer it properly.
Yes, ojel? If you want something, say it plainly. I was reading.

Jazbay, lavender and juniper grow together just north-west of here. An alchemist would find them useful. I would sooner see them gathered by a herbalist who knows the difference between them. Precisely.
You ask about Black Marsh. Ask Flaa Heet how Lilmoth is governed. I would have written it down myself, but the tree-minders of Lilmoth refused to let me sit by the city's Hist and take notes.
I am Heem-Tsal. I cast fire for this band and read whatever I can get my claws on. I travel with them for the passage south. I have not yet found a reason to leave.
If you want a book, there is a bookseller, Looks-At-Books, who keeps her shelf at Hereguard Plantation, a fair way west of here. I have heard of that shelf, and I intend to see it.
More dead walk among the gravestones north of Lilmoth's walls, a short way north-west of here. And a crocodile lies in the water a short way west of us. Why would you go near either?
You. Good. Stand by me a moment. The track is quiet. I would like it to stay so.
You there. What do you want? Keep your hands where I can see them.
The dead trees on the shore track stand just north-east of here. The band camps among them. Why do you ask?
I carry a blade in each hand. I keep the band's watch. I was a guard once. I will not tell you for whom.

Two Argonians loiter by the leeks to the north. Sheeh-Vos is just north-north-east, and Waits-For-Lanterns just north-east. I do not trust either of them. You there, what business do you have with them?
Flaa Heet, is it? Walk south-west a short way, till you come to the rowing boat. Then keep to the shore, south-west, another short way. The village is there.
The dock? Look, fellow, it is just there, north-north-east, in plain sight. I have stared at it long enough to know.
Ahh, my friend, my friend. Sit down and tell me you brought something to wet the throat. I will tell you about the boat again, if you will have it.
Hm? Oh. What do you want, fellow? I am only sitting.
Black Marsh is wide. I have seen only the water of it. There is a big ship tied up at the dock now, with steps going down beside it to the water. I watched them load her, I did, every crate.
There are three dead Dunmer lying at the east end of the dock, a short way north-north-east of here. They have not been buried. I do not go near, but I notice who does.
Deep-In-His-Cups, they call me. I earned it. I was a boatman once, and I lost my boat. Sit a while and I will tell you how, fellow.
Come close, friend. Keep your voice low, eh? I know you. The dock is quiet.
Hsst. Do not stand over me, cousin. I am only picking leeks.
Leeks? They grow right here, and more just west-south-west. Take what you like, but stay low while you do it.
Past the bodies at the east end of the dock there is a chest, a short way east-north-east, eh? It is worth a look before anyone else gets there.
Dunmer lie there as well, just north-east of here. They have not been looted yet. Keep quiet on the way.
I am Sheeh-Vos. I gather what the dock loses. I do not ask who owned it. Do not look at my hands for too long.
Deep-In-His-Cups sits just south-south-east of here, eh? He sees everything at the dock and remembers half of it. Ask him, not me.
Walking Dead wander outside the walls, honoured guest. Go a short way north-west and you will meet them. I would not hurry there.
Ah. You came back, my friend. Stand here beside me, where the shadows are good, and tell me what you have seen.
Honoured guest. You speak to me in plain sight, which I would not have chosen. Say what you want, slowly.
A hungry man can eat on this shore. There are gourds growing a short way west-south-west of here. Take what you need.
There is a door below the walls, a short way west-north-west of here. It leads indoors and is out of the way. I will say no more than that.
There is a thing I know. I do not give it to a stranger, honoured guest. Come back when I have had cause to trust you. Perhaps I will speak then.

Near the graves north of the walls, a short way north-west of here, there is a trapdoor in the ground. It leads down under the city. The chest beside it has already been emptied, so do not expect a reward.

I am Waits-For-Lanterns. I plan small jobs and I wait for dark to do them. It is a slow season, honoured guest, nothing more. I stand nearest the dock, where I can count the lanterns and the guards between them.
The big ship, traveller? Keep to the boards and head south a short way. It is there, you cannot miss it. I would sooner be posted at that dock than here.
Temple Pass is north, traveller. Take the path north a short way, until the dead tree is on your right. Then cross the open ground north a fair way, and you are at Temple Pass.
Oh, good, it is you! Stand with me a while. Ukka-Meesh has told me another story, and I want to tell it to you.
Be well, traveller. Do you have a question?
Tidings, traveller. I am on watch here, so speak quickly.
This is the middle of Thorn, traveller. The signpost is right beside me, to the south-west.
Who founded Thorn? Ask Ma-Veesk, traveller. Ukka-Meesh has told me some of it, but Ma-Veesk can tell it to you properly.
I am Xeech-Nu, traveller. I am new to the watch, and I listen to the stories of Ukka-Meesh, a guard here. I would like a post on the docks.
Ukka-Meesh is a guard at the centre, like me, traveller. He is just east of here.
I am a guard at the town's centre, traveller. New guards are posted to the centre until someone trusts them. I would rather be on the south dock.
Ah, it is you. Sit a while, my friend. I am only half awake, but I am glad of the company.
Mm. Yes, traveller? Speak slowly. I have been on watch a long time.
I keep watch over the east houses with Jeelus-Vax, traveller. The house lies just north-north-west of here.
Ask Tolyn Vedram about the painting of the Slave-Coffles, traveller. I have seen it too, and I do not like to speak of it.
I am Sleeps-Standing, traveller. I earned the name on a long watch. I guard the east houses.
Severan Otho, the hired Imperial soldier, stands just south-south-east of here, traveller.
I guard the east houses. The watch changes twice a day, traveller. The night is long.
Thorn, outlander? Follow the path south-west a short way, until the dead tree stands on your right. Then go south, and Thorn is just there.
I need not ask whose side you are on. Sit. I will see to the Owings after we talk.
Outlander. Whose side are you on?
There is a house just east of here. Look, but do not trouble the people in it. Whose side are you on, outlander?
Heita-Meen? Fendyl Omoren is the one to ask, outlander. I know that story by heart, and I will tell it once I know whose side you are on.
Ask Jeelus-Vax about the title, outlander, though I think of Jeelus-Vax as a collar with a spear. The rising means to settle that title on those who work it.
I am Owes-Nothing. I took that name the day I walked off an Owing, and I fight for those who stood in Thorn when the Dres left.
Tallies-Twice is a Tax Heel, one of the field-owners' collectors of Owings and tolls. That thief is just north of here.
I am a soldier of the rising. We want every Owing in Thorn ended, and the title settled on those who work it.

State your business first, citizen. Then hear this. A giant crab, Old Salty, lives in the shallows just east-south-east of this bench. Giant mudcrabs sit on the shore a short way east-north-east. Keep clear of both.

Soulrest? Attend, citizen. Go north-east a short way, until Lilmoth is on your right. Then east, another short way, until the burnt-out house is on your left. Then south-east a short way, to Lilmoth Dock. From there, ask again. Soulrest lies further east.
You again, my friend. Good. The watch is quiet. Stand easy and I will tell you if that changes.
Halt, citizen. State your business. Keep your hands clear of your weapon.
I am Hard-Scale. I am a soldier in the pay of the Lilmoth council. I guard the south side of Hereguard, where the crop is grown. Nothing happens here while I stand watch.
Rakhee-Tul stands just north of this bench. He holds the easier post. He sleeps on it. Report to him if you must, citizen. Do not expect much.
If your gear needs tightening, boss, there is an armour workbench just north-north-east of here. Use it before you go wandering, not after.
Mind the fly amanita, boss. It grows just west-south-west of here. You do not want to eat it.
Well, look who it is. Come over, my friend. There is shade here and Hard-Scale is not looking. Sit a while.
Hm. New face, boss. Whatever you want, make it quick. I am on duty and Hard-Scale likes to count.
There is a beached ship a short way south of here. Iron and leather armour, weapons, a silver plate and a captain's journal lie by it. I am only saying, boss.
A passage door near that ship leads in, a short way south of here. Do not tell Hard-Scale you heard it from me.
Rakhee-Tul. The Lilmoth council pays me to guard the south side of this plantation with Hard-Scale. I took the post for the pay. I will not pretend otherwise.
You have come back, my friend. Sit out of the rain and read something. I have kept the dry volumes for you.
Reader. Mind the pages, and keep your wet hands off the stock.

Once, a foreigner without a licence was kept to the docks of Lilmoth and barred from the city. Ask Lifts-The-Sacks how a debt is settled here. I only sell to the house, and its steward pays me a season late.
I am Looks-At-Books. I came to Hereguard because the steward buys paper for the ledgers, and I read everything I sell before I sell it. Look at my fingers if you doubt me.

I sell books, paper and writing things. There are the four volumes of The Argonian Account, The Lusty Argonian Maid, volumes 1 and 2, The Sultry Argonian Bard, volume 1, Short History of Morrowind and Welcome to Black Marsh. I also have rolls of paper, inkwells and quills. I would rather sell The Argonian Account together than one volume at a time.
Neeta-Lei keeps the house, just east of here. She is good company.
I sell books from the tables on the west side of the plantation house, under cover, because damp ruins stock faster than thieves. The house has a bed just east-south-east of here.
Easy water, traveller, but keep your eyes open to the south-south-east. A bear and her cubs roam a short way off that way, and a Tree Mother lives in the woods there too. Stay clear of both.
The Dwemer Ruin, traveller? Easy enough. Walk south-east from here a short way and you are standing in it.

Alten Merihall, traveller? Walk south-east a short way, until the Dwemer Ruin is on your left, and then keep south-east a fair way. Alten Merihall is there, and the money with it. If you would rather go by water, I can take you.
Lilmoth Dock, traveller? Walk west a short way, until the big ship is on your left, and then climb west a fair way. The dock is there.
Easy water, my friend! Sit by me a while. There is room on the landing. I chose Soulrest over Lilmoth Dock because there is no licence to be shown here. Now I have good company besides.
Easy water, traveller. This is Soulrest, and I run a boat from the landing here. Where are you going, and do you need a boat to get there?
Soulrest is where the boats tie up, traveller. Mine is one of them. A large ship lies west of here, a short way to the west-south-west, with a door aboard if you want to look inside.

Lilmoth fell, traveller. The outside traders went elsewhere after that. Alten Merihall's merchants have taken much of the bay's trade since then. That is where the money is now. I would carry you there gladly.

Heavy-Rope leads a crew on Soulrest's dock. The crew want their season ended early, traveller. The broker who hires them out will not hear of it. I only watch from the landing, so go and ask Heavy-Rope yourself.
I am Seeks-The-Channel, and I run a boat out of Soulrest, east of Lilmoth Dock. I wait here at the head of the landing between fares. I chose this place because no licence is asked for here.
You are back, my friend. Come to the stall. I will sell you what I have at last season's price, and not a coin more.
Outsider. Buy something or move along. Do not touch the goods.
Gourds grow just north-north-west of this stall. Pick your own. Mine are for sale.
This is Soulrest. Houses open onto it, one just south of me and another just south-east. Keep your hands off the doors, outsider.
I am Ushaa-Mei. I sell food here on the south-west side, between the houses. I remember what everything cost last season, so do not try to argue.
Food and small goods. I sell them at last season's price. I weigh it fair and I expect the coin to be good.
Plaits-The-Reed sits just west of me. I like her. Ask her yourself.
Hello again! Sit by the fire with me, and I will tell you what the grown-ups said today.
Hello, sir. Or miss. Please, do you smile?
Deathbell, nightshade, jazbay and other flowers grow together, miss. They are just south-east of here.
This is Soulrest, sir. Two cows graze just east-north-east of here, and Cow-Chaser scares them on purpose. Then he says it was me.
I am Little-Gecko. I sit in the middle, sir, where the grown-ups talk, so I hear everything. One day I will be a boat captain.
Seeks-The-Channel, the boat captain, stands just east of here. She is the best captain there is. Feldril Nethri, the Dunmer, works just north-east. He is kind to me, miss.
A Vale Deer lies dead just south-east of here, child. Something killed it. I would not go looking for the cause.
Child, you came back. Sit by me, out of the wind, and let me look at your hands. Tell me how you are.
Mind the reeds, child. I have not finished with them yet.
Glowing mushrooms and creep cluster grow under the trees, a short way south of here, child. I do not go that far now.
An Argonian kept long from the Hist grows pale, child. The colour thins and the markings go soft. When they go home, it all comes back.
Careful hands are sometimes of use to Tilts-The-Jug, child. Inside the house on Soulrest's dock, I am told. I always look at a stranger's hands first. Let me see yours.
I am Plaits-The-Reed. I weave mats and baskets for the families here, and for the boats. My husband is out fishing, child. He will be back soon.
Xeeh-Nah works just east-south-east of here. Xeeh-Nah should marry, I always say. Go and see, child.
Warrior! You are here! Did you bring the sword? Show me, show me, I will not touch it.
Hey, warrior! Have you got a sword? Do you have any scars? Show me one!
Gourds? They grow just north-west of here, warrior. I could carry them all myself, but I am busy with the cows.
This is Soulrest, and I am the best fighter in it! Ask the cows. A boar roots a short way north-east of here, and I am going to fight it one day.
I am Cow-Chaser, a hatchling of Soulrest, and I am going to be a warrior! I practise on the cows, because they run and that makes them hard to hit. Do you have a real sword?
Little-Gecko sits just west-south-west of here. Little-Gecko is a baby. Xeeh-Nah works just south of here. Xeeh-Nah is the strongest person alive! Go and see for yourself, warrior.

Go north-west a fair way, until Lilmoth Dock is on your left. Climb west a short way to the big ship on your left. Then west again, a short way, to the dead tree on your left. From there, ask again, ojel. The plantation lies further west.
Kin. Good. Sit by the benches a while. I will move the loads later.
Mm. What do you want, ojel? I have loads to move.
There is a chest by the big ship. It is a short way west-south-west of here. I do not know more than that.
On the big docks they hire a ship's crew with another man's months of owing. The harbourmaster calls it hiring. Free hands lose their paid work to it.
Tilts-The-Jug sometimes wants careful hands, ojel. Mine are for hauling. Try the house on the dock.
I am Xeeh-Nah. I haul cargo and tie up the boats here at Soulrest, on the south-east side. Half the people of Soulrest owe me money.
I carry loads and tie the boats up. The big ship lies a short way west of here. Its door leads aboard.
Ah, it is you. Few people trouble to cross to this end of the room. I do not forget the ones who do. Stay a while, friend.
Well, outlander. You have found the corner of Soulrest where visitors do not come by choice. State your business and I shall tell you whether I can oblige.

This is Soulrest, outlander. I am not permitted by the fire with the families, so I am put at this end. The north door is just west of me and another just east-south-east. The cooking pot stands just south-east, though I would not say I am welcome to it.

Here a debt is paid in work, outlander. An arbitrator turns the loss into months of labour that are counted in nushmeekos. When the months are worked the matter is over, so they say. Once, foreigners without a licence were kept to the docks at Lilmoth and barred from the city.

The crew that Heavy-Rope leads works Soulrest's dock, outlander. They want their season ended early. The broker who hires out their labour refuses. I was a trader once, and I know a broker's terms win over a man's wishes. Ask for Heavy-Rope there.

I am Feldril Nethri, a Dunmer. For now I am a guest of this marsh, though the hospitality has terms. I came to trade. I lost a cargo and was assessed months of labour. I cannot see when they will end, outlander.
There is a child called Little-Gecko, sitting just south-west of here. She is kind to me, which is more than I can say for most under this roof. I would thank you not to trouble her.
Sit on the bench, tall one. It is about ten paces south-east of here. Why are you still standing? Are your feet tired?

Longmont? Why do you want to go there? Walk south-east about sixty paces to the bamboo hut on your right. Then follow the shore south-east, a long way, about a hundred and seventy-five paces, until the giant tree is on your right. Walk east from there about a hundred and sixty-five paces. Longmont is there.
You came back, my friend! Did you come through the water or dry? Tell me everything. I counted you in.
You, tall one. Who are you? Where did you come from? Did you walk through the water? I saw your feet.
Lily pads? They float on the water west of here. Some are seven paces off. More are ten paces west-south-west. Why do you want them? Can you swim?
This is Low-Reed Village. I know every face in it. The rowing boat lies on the water thirteen paces west of here. It is mine to guard. Do not touch it, tall one.
I am Ree-Nakka. I am a hatchling of this village. I mind the rowing boat. Who comes and who goes? I count them all. Who are you counting?

Mends-The-Nets works east-south-east of here, about twenty paces. That is the cleverest person in the village. Ixa-Mee plays about twenty-two paces east. Ixa-Mee is a tattler. Keep your secrets from that one.

Stranger. Walk east round the cliffs about ninety paces to the giant tree. Then walk west over open ground, about six hundred and fifty paces, until the burnt-out house is on your left. Walk west about three hundred and fifty paces from there, and the ruin is in front of you.
It is you. I am glad, my friend. I will not whisper this time.
Stranger. Your hands are empty. That is good.
Stranger. I am not to talk long. Please say what you need.
Lily pads float east-south-east of here, stranger, about twenty-five paces off. Take them yourself.
This is Low-Reed Village. There is a bamboo hut about twenty paces north of here with a bed roll in it. I sleep there.
I am Ixa-Mee, stranger. I was hatched here in Low-Reed Village, as was everyone I know.
Mends-The-Nets sits about nine paces south-west of here. Mends-The-Nets is kind to me.
I fetch for Mends-The-Nets, stranger. The village workbench is about sixteen paces north of here.
Alten Merihall, traveller. Walk south-west about 175 paces until the giant tree is on your right. Then go west over open ground about 500 paces to reach it.
Longmont is a plain way, traveller. Walk south-east about 200 paces until the giant tree is on your right, then walk east about 170 paces to reach it.
There is room by the nets. Sit while I work, friend. A knot holds better when two people talk over it.
Speak, traveller. My hands will keep working while you do.
This is Low-Reed Village, traveller. Two giant trees stand near here, one about 50 paces south-south-east and one about 58 paces east-south-east. I have never wanted to live anywhere else.
A root-herald speaks for a village to outsiders. News, trade and terms all go through that one, traveller.
Turns-The-Clutch is the egg-tender of this village. Turns-The-Clutch keeps the clutch.
I am Mends-The-Nets. I have mended this village's nets since I was small. Half the villagers learned their knots from me.
Ixa-Mee is about 9 paces north-east of here. I am fond of that one. Ree-Nakka is about 20 paces west-north-west. That one will lead this village or ruin it.
I mend nets, traveller. The benches stand about 4 paces north-east of here and 11 paces west. The workbench is about 23 paces north-north-east. I would mend a frayed strap of yours as well.

The Dwemer ruin. Follow the shore north about a hundred and ten paces until the giant tree stands on your left. Then climb west over open ground about three hundred and sixty paces until the burnt-out house stands on your left. Then west about three hundred and fifty paces more. Walk softly, walker.
Alten Merihall. Go south-west about two hundred and thirty paces until the giant tree stands on your right. Then west over open ground some four hundred and fifty paces. The hall is there.
Ah, my friend. Sit by the water with me. The water is calm today.
Walker. Keep your voice low. The fish listen.
Walker. Step quietly on the bank.
Lily pads lie thick on the water to the south-east, a few paces off. Take them gently, walker. Do not splash.
The giant trees stand west-south-west and north-north-west of me, a little way off. I think they hear more than we know.
When two of us quarrel here, they choose one that both of them trust to hear it. Most often that is the tree-minder. Pays-Late holds that place now. I trust Pays-Late above all.
I am Xeech-Utsei. I fish this still water with a pole. It takes patience, walker.
Hulee-Tah is south-south-west of here, not far off. He is loud. Keep him away from my water.

Alten Merihall? Go south-west along the shore, some hundred and eighty paces, to the giant tree on your right. From the tree strike west over open ground, about four hundred and fifty paces. Alten Merihall is there, outsider.

Longmont is easy. Walk south-east about a hundred paces until you reach the giant tree. Then follow the shore east about two hundred and sixty paces, until the rowing boat lies on your right. Then walk east about a hundred paces. Longmont is there.
Ha! You came back, my friend. Stand by my hut and tell me what you have seen.
Outsider! You walk up to a man at his work. Speak, but mind the bamboo.
My hut is about seven paces west of here, with a bed roll inside. I built it first. I built it best. Out on the water, east-north-east about twenty-six paces, lies a rowing boat.
Ask Mends-The-Nets about the root-herald. I only know that I would trade for less than any herald, and I say so loudly.
I am Hulee-Tah. I build and patch the bamboo huts of this village, my own first. I went once to trade at the road-houses. I came home sure that we do things better here.
Jaa-Kur is about eighteen paces south-east of here and helps me when I build. Xeech-Utsei is about thirty-three paces north-north-east. You will find Xeech-Utsei idle.
I build bamboo huts. I want enough bamboo to raise a second one before the rains, outsider. A giant tree stands about twenty-six paces north-west of here, as a mark for steering.
Big one, there is a bench about thirty paces east-north-east of here. Bamboo is heavy and I sit on it when my arms are tired.

Longmont? Go south-east, ninety paces or so, to the giant tree. Keep it on your right. Then follow the shore east about three hundred paces to the dead tree, also on your right. Then walk east about eighty paces more. Longmont is there.
Big one, big one, I am so glad! I kept the shallows warm for you. Did you bring something shiny this time?
Hello, big one. What did you bring with you?
There are lily pads about three paces west-south-west of here and about three paces east. They float in the shallows where I play.

This is the village and I carry bamboo here when there is bamboo to carry. There is a rowing boat out on the water, north-north-east about twenty-four paces from here. Ree-Nakka is bossy and will not let me near it.
I am Jaa-Kur and I am the youngest hatchling here. I follow the hut-builder and carry whatever I am given. One day I will carry the long poles.
Hulee-Tah is by his hut, about eighteen paces north-west of here. He is the best of all of us and I want to be just like him.
The Way to Ruins? Walk north-east about two hundred and thirty-five paces. You will see it.
You came back. Good. Sit on the bench with me, because my feet have had enough for today.
You there. If you want something hauled, say so. I have lines to pull.

There is a bench about twenty paces east-north-east of here. An iron door about thirty-four paces north-east leads indoors. The houses are further off, about sixty-four paces south-south-east and sixty-seven paces east-south-east.
The Panther River forks near Helstrom. I grew up on it, so I know it well.
You there. Haj-Wan wants an outsider to go after her kin Sei-Wan, who walked out into the basin alone. She waits at Helstrom's gate. I haul lines and nothing else, so I keep out of it.
I am Hauls-Wet-Rope. The dock bosses gave me that name and I kept it. I came down the Panther River for the work.
Namorine is about twenty-three paces south of here. You will find her on the easy loads. Do not ask me to walk you there.
I haul the lines and the loads for whoever pays, here at the north end. A Dwemer ruin rises about forty paces south of here, so you cannot miss the place. Look at my hands if you doubt the work.

The Way to Ruins? Walk north-east for about two hundred and sixty-six paces. That is the way, passenger. If you want the other place, Gih-Xaleel, follow the path south for about two hundred and thirty-four paces.
Well, look who has come back! Sit with me a while, my friend. I have been waiting by these ruins. You are better company than the water.
Passenger? Are you looking for a boat? I wait here for anyone who wants carrying along the water. Tell me where you are bound and I will tell you what it costs.

This is Helstrom, and I think it is the finest city there is. The Dwemer ruins rise just south of here, the nearer about sixteen paces off and the farther about thirty-three. There are iron doors too, about forty-two paces south-west and forty-four south-east, if you want to go indoors.
Many people call Helstrom the immortal capital of the Argonians. I say they are right. I have seen other places on my fares, and no other place compares.
Rumours? Helstrom and Stormhold have been rivals for a long time. I carried fares as far as the Stormhold side once. The people there haggled me down every time, so I do not go back.
I am Namorine, the boatman. I wait here by the ruins for a fare. My mother gave me this name and I have kept it, though the people of Helstrom cannot place it. Ask me about the water if you like.
Hauls-Wet-Rope works about twenty-three paces north of here. He works too hard. Bejeen-Ul stands about seventy-five paces south. I like his company, so tell him Namorine sent you.
If you need to sit, visitor, there is a bench about twenty paces south-south-east of here. Sit on it and keep your weight off the old walls.

Climb south about one hundred and seventy paces, until the waterfall is on your left. Then walk south-west some two hundred and eighty paces to the bridge on your left. Follow the shore south-west about eighty paces to the old stone columns on your left, then follow the shore south about a hundred paces more. Helstrom is there.
Welcome, my friend. Sit with me by the stone for a while. I am glad of your company.
Visitor. Mind the wall. It is old, so do not lean on it.

A Dwemer ruin stands right beside us, about two paces east-south-east. Another stands a little way north-north-east. Houses stand to the west, about thirty paces and forty paces on, with an iron door about twenty paces west.
Ask Namorine what they call Helstrom. I like her talk. I think the city is older than anyone's story of it.
Haj-Wan waits at Helstrom's gate, visitor. Her kin Sei-Wan went into the basin by himself. She asks for an outsider to follow him. I patch walls and cannot leave them, but I hope an outsider goes.
I am Bejeen-Ul. I patch the old stonework in these streets for the assembly's levy. The assembly pays me late. I like stone that does not crumble when I touch it.
Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden, keeps the gate about ninety paces south of here. He is fair, visitor.
The alleys of Helstrom are counted both wonderful and dangerous, outlander. Keep your weapon sheathed in them and your eyes open.

Helstrom? Climb south-west about forty paces to the waterfall on your left. Then south-west about three hundred paces to the bridge on your left. Then the shore: south-west about eighty paces, past the old stone columns, keeping them on your left. After that, south along the shore about a hundred and ten paces. Helstrom is there.
Way to Ruins? Follow the path north about two hundred paces to the old stone columns on your right. Then walk north-east about three hundred paces. It is there.
Your face is known here and I have no complaint of you. The gate is quiet. Go through.
Outlander. State your business at this gate.
This is the gate of Helstrom, outlander. Dwemer ruins stand about six paces south of me and seven north-north-west. A stone tower stands about twenty-three paces east-south-east.
A waterfall falls about thirty-three paces south-west of here. Two bridges cross the water near it, about thirty-four paces south-south-west and south-west. Do not wander far from the path.
Helstrom has never been taken by an army. After the Battle of Argonia the Empire never tried. The Imperial historians call our guard brutes. I do not care what they write.
I am Gih-Xaleel, a warden of Helstrom's levy. I keep this gate and I decide who goes in. Helstrom has never been taken, and I mean to see it stays so.
I sell nothing. I keep the gate. An iron door stands about thirty paces north-north-west of here. It leads into a hall where a soldier of the levy stands guard.
Sells-Dear the boat captain is about a hundred and fifteen paces west of here. Weesa-Nur is about a hundred paces west-south-west. Sells-Dear is sharp but honest.

Helstrom? Count with me. Walk south-west 180 paces to the bridge on your left. Follow the shore south-west 80 paces to the old stone columns on your left. Then follow the shore south 111 paces. Helstrom is there.
Gih-Xaleel keeps his post. Follow the shore north 155 paces. He is there.
You are back, my friend. I have counted every crate since you left. The count is better with you here. What do you carry today?
Newcomer. I count what comes off the boats. I also count who walks off with it. What do you carry, and how heavy is it?

Look at the old stone columns, 27 paces north-east of here. There is an iron door 14 paces south-south-east that leads indoors. A house stands 34 paces south-south-west. That is all I count in this spot.

Newcomer. A beast in the shallows took one of the landing crew, and no raft has gone out since. I count nothing off the rafts until one does. Okan-Zish of that crew is by the stone tower at the landing, and he wants it dealt with.
I am Counts-Every-Crate. I took a city name for city work. I was born in the interior. There a sack of food is worth more to me than a purse. How many sacks do you carry, newcomer?
Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden, keeps his post 109 paces north of here. He is exact. I respect that. Go to him if you need a man who keeps order.

I carry and count what is landed at the dock. It is 26 paces west-north-west of here. In the deep interior food, tools and safe passage are worth more than coin. I still think so. Show me what you carry, newcomer.

Helstrom? Walk south-west about eighty paces, until the bridge is on your left. Follow the shore south-west another eighty, past the old stone columns on your left. Then keep to the shore south for a hundred and ten paces or so, and there it is.
Sit, my friend. The bench is long enough for two. The bridges are quiet.
Well, walker. What brings you to my bridges?
Two bridges, walker. One is about seventeen paces south-west, the other twenty south. The bench is five paces south-east. A house stands beyond it, twenty-nine paces east.
Taken? Helstrom has never been taken by an army. After the Battle of Argonia, the Empire never tried again.
I am a soldier of Helstrom's levy, walker. I came out of the marsh to serve. I will go back to it. Until then I watch the bridges from here.
Azum-Kai? He keeps watch at the stone tower, seventy-four paces south-west. He is keener than the post needs.
I watch who crosses the bridges, and how often. There is a dock forty-eight paces south-east, if you want boats instead.

Helstrom is close. Follow the shore south about one hundred and eight paces, past the old stone columns, until you see the boat on its rack on your left. Then follow the shore south-west about twenty-eight paces. Helstrom is there.

The Dwarven Ruins lie beyond Helstrom. Follow the shore south about one hundred and forty paces past the old stone columns until Helstrom is on your right. Go along the boards south-east about one hundred and thirty-four paces until the big ship is on your right. Then climb south-east over open ground about five hundred and twelve paces until the standing stone is on your left. Then follow the shore south-east about one hundred and seventy-six paces to the ruins.
It is good to see you again, my friend. The watch has been quiet since you left. I have kept it carefully.
Halt, traveller. State your business at the stone tower.
Traveller. This is the levy watch. What brings you here?
A bridge crosses the water about sixteen paces north of here. South of here an iron door leads indoors, about thirty-one paces away. Old stone columns stand about twenty-eight paces south-west.
There is a bridge about sixteen paces north. The iron door about thirty-one paces south leads indoors. I do not know what you want with it, traveller.
Helstrom's guard has a name for being dangerous. I know that name well. I mean to deserve one like it here.
I am a soldier and not a scholar of the province, traveller. I do know that Helstrom's guard has a name for being dangerous. The soldiers of the levy respect it.

Traveller, from this tower I watch the rafters sit idle. A beast in the shallows has taken one of their crew, and no raft has gone out since. Ask Okan-Zish, who stands near the tower here. He wants it dealt with.
I am Azum-Kai, a soldier of the levy. I keep the watch at this tower, and I take that duty seriously.
I took this post young. I keep the levy's watch here in full uniform. There is little else to say about me, traveller.
The rafters Okan-Zish and Wuleen-Taza stand about twelve paces west-north-west and nine paces north-west of here. I do not trust either of them. I watch them closely.
I am a soldier of the levy. The stone tower stands about two paces west-south-west of here, and I keep its watch. Benches flank it, about three paces south-east and six paces west.
I serve the levy at the stone tower, two paces west-south-west of where we stand. Benches stand beside it, about three paces south-east and six paces west.
Helstrom, dry-foot? I know that shore better than any boat captain. Follow the shore south about a hundred and fifty paces. That is Helstrom.
Good, a face I know. Stay a while and watch the water with me, friend. Trade is slow, but the company is better.
Dry-foot. If you need a crossing, my raft is the best on this water. Nothing bigger is worth the trust.
This is the landing. I work it. There is an iron door about forty paces west-south-west that leads indoors. Houses with doors stand north past the bridge, sixty or seventy paces off.
My people, the Agaceph, travel on thin rafts made for one, pushed along by the tail. I have never trusted anything bigger. For Helstrom and the Empire, ask Teeka-Xul.
I am Okan-Zish, an Agaceph rafter. I pole goods across this water with Wuleen-Taza, when the water lets us.
Wuleen-Taza is a few paces east-north-east of here. I stand by that one in everything. Azum-Kai the soldier is about a dozen paces east-south-east. He watches us too closely.
There is a bench about seven paces south of here. Sit there, customer, if you need to rest.

Cross the bridge and go north-east about sixty paces. Then walk north-east about two hundred and thirty paces, until the waterfall is on your left. After that, follow the path north about two hundred and seventy paces, until the old stone columns are on your right. Then go north-east about two hundred and eighty paces to reach the Way to Ruins.
Customer, I know you now. Sit with me a while. We can do business later.
Customer. What do you want?
A bridge crosses about ten paces north-east of here. The stone tower stands nearly as close, to the south-south-east.
Ask Okan-Zish about the Agaceph and their rafts. He talks of them for free, customer. I do not give things away.
I am Wuleen-Taza, Agaceph, from the deep interior. I do the bargaining for the crew, because Okan-Zish is a poor bargainer.
Okan-Zish is a few paces west-south-west of here. He is a fool. I look after him. Teeka-Xul the soldier sits about seventy paces north-east. He is harmless.
Okan-Zish and I pole a raft on the water here. I do the bargaining. Ask Counts-Every-Crate about coin in the deep interior. I will weigh what you offer, customer, in coin or in kind.
The dock? Follow the shore south-east for a hundred and thirty-five paces or so. It is there. Mind where you put your feet on the way.
You again, my friend. Come in, but wipe your boots first. I will not have mud tracked through my house, not even by you.
Well. Look at the state of those boots. What do you want on my doorstep?

That is my door, eight paces west of you. The house itself is a little further, fourteen paces west-north-west. Keep off the step. There is a stone tower thirty-eight paces south-west, and a Dwemer ruin fifty paces east. Why are you asking?
Rumours? Ask Namorine about Helstrom and Stormhold. I hear plenty from my doorstep, but I do not give it away. The dock folk are thieves who sell it dear.
I keep this house. I have lived in Helstrom all my life. I sell what I can spare to the boats at the dock. Now, who are you?
Sells-Dear, the boat captain, stands forty-four paces north-north-west of here. He ties up too close to my house. Tell him I said so.

I sell what I can spare to the boats at the dock. A bridge crosses sixty-four paces east of here, and the dock is eighty-five paces south-east. Count your change there, because the dock folk are all thieves.

Ruins, buyer? Climb east some seventy paces to the stone tower. Then follow the path north-east about two hundred and fifty paces, until the old stone columns are on your right. Walk north-east another three hundred paces or so, and you are at Way to Ruins. I charge nothing for that walk. Hah.

The Dwarven Ruins will cost you good boots. Walk south about three hundred paces, until the stone tower is on your right. Then follow the shore south a hundred and fifty paces, until Helstrom is on your right. Then take the boards south another hundred and fifty paces, until the big ship is on your left. From there, ask again. The ruins lie further south-east. Hah.
Ah, I know that purse. For you the first price is the last price, friend. I will not even laugh while I say it.
Buyer! You look like you carry coin. Tell me what you need. I will tell you what it costs. Hah.
See the door close by, five paces to the west-north-west? That is a house, about fifteen paces on to the north-west. A second door is some forty paces east. Hah.
A Dwemer ruin rises thirty paces to the north-north-east. Keep clear of it, buyer, unless you can pay for the trouble. Hah.
I am Sells-Dear. I run a boat out of Helstrom and I trade by it. I took a city name, because city buyers pay a city price to a city name. Hah.
Weesa-Nur lives about fifty-five paces south-south-east of here. Be careful, buyer. She is a busybody who will count your coin before you do. Hah.
I trade by boat. Okan-Zish and Wuleen-Taza work the landing, some two hundred and fifty paces south of here. They tell every customer I cheat them. I say they should buy a boat of their own. Hah.
Out in the deep interior food, tools and safe passage are worth more than coin. Remember that, buyer, when you are hungry and a boat is the only road. Hah.
Thorn, civilian? Go north, a hundred and ninety-odd paces, and you're in the town's centre square.
Stand easy. The ship's quiet and the men are paid.
State your business, civilian. I've men to pay and a ship to mind.
Well, civilian? Say it plainly, I haven't the time for talk.
These are the south docks. The big ship is about a dozen paces east of here, and I'd keep clear of it.
Thorn's name? Ask Bites-The-Coin, civilian. I keep my men paid and in order, and I've no more to say about the town.
That's not for a stranger. I'll say it once, civilian. There's cargo behind the ship's door, twenty paces east, that's on no tally. Repeat it and you'll answer to me.
Aulus Varrenius, sergeant. I lead a company that came on the big ship and hires out to the field-owners hereabouts. We serve no Empire; there's been none here for two centuries.
Decimus Pell, archer of my company, is three paces south-south-east. Ask him what you like, civilian. Keep it short.
It's you. Good. Stand where I can see the wind on you and tell me what you need.
Stranger. State your business, and keep your hands where I can see them.
You want the dock, stranger? It's about twenty paces north-east of here.
Those who defend the Owing say it's theirs. It came from their own arbitration, and it ends. A prison doesn't. I'd call that fair.
Decimus Pell. I came with Aulus Varrenius's company, and I guard the ship with a bow. I keep to myself, stranger.
Quintus Albero. Young soldier of our company. A dozen paces east-north-east of here. You'll hear him before you reach him.
I'm an archer. The company guards whoever pays it, and the field-owners pay now. That's the whole of it, stranger.
Oh, I was hoping you'd come by! It's good to talk to someone who isn't in the company. I'll tell you, I've been thinking of home all morning.
Good day, sir or madam. Is there something I can do for you? I'm only one of the soldiers, mind, so I may not know much.
Oh! Hello. Sorry, I didn't see you there. What can I do for you?
This place? Truth be told, I'm still working out what to make of it; it's nothing like home. There's a door about five paces east of here, if that's what you're after.
The Empire's been gone from Black Marsh for two hundred years, sir. Imperial people stayed on, but the flag didn't, and I'd gone and thought I was joining the Legion.
Black Marsh? Two hundred years the Empire's been gone from it, they tell me. Plenty of our own people stayed on, but you won't find our flag, and I do keep looking for it.
Me? Quintus Albero, sir, the youngest in the company. I miss home something terrible. I can't stop talking about it, as you'll have noticed.
If it's someone from the company you want, our corporal, Marius Lentulo, is about ten paces north-north-east of here, sir.

I'm with the hired company, sir. We sign on for a season and are paid at the end of it; not what I pictured when I put my name down, I'll admit. Decimus Pell, one of the company, still calls me 'boy', and he's cold with it.
Thorn? Follow the boards north-west, a hundred and eighty paces or so, and you'll be standing in the square. Hard to miss, traveller.
Well, you know the dock by now. Mind the boards, the tide has them wet. I've a minute, if you want it.
Traveller. What can I do for you? Quickly, if you can; I've stores to see to.
Well, traveller. State your business, or let me get on. I cannot stop the tide for either of us.
The dock? A dozen paces north-north-west of where I'm standing, traveller. Watch the tide on the planks.
The Empire? Quintus Albero is the one to ask, traveller. I know it's gone and I don't miss it. I've stores to see to.
Marius Lentulo, corporal in Aulus Varrenius's company, and its quartermaster. My grandfather was a Legion man. I'm a hired man, traveller. I carry no flag.
