Aulus Varrenius, sergeant of our hired company, is about eighteen paces south-west of here. I trust him, which is more than I say of most.
I'm the company's quartermaster. We keep our stores on the ship and sell what we can't eat, traveller. All I ask is that supplies come in on time.
The big ship? Head south along the boards, sixty-seven paces or so, until it's on your right. Then keep on south-east along the boards another fifty-four, and there it is.
You'll want the big ship. Go south along the boards, a little over sixty paces, till it's on your right; after that, south-east along the boards for fifty-odd paces and you're at it.
Stop a while and tell me how you've been; I've no one else to talk to about nothing in particular.
Come and stand with me a moment; there's no hurry. I'm glad of the talk.
Good day, traveller. That's an accent I can't quite place. What can I do for you?
Traveller. Keep to the boards and you'll come to no harm. Something I can help with?
Not much to it from where I stand, traveller. The dock's about twenty-five paces south-south-east of here, if that's what you're after.
Ask Quintus Albero about the Empire, traveller; I can't tell you much of it. I was born here. Black Marsh is the only home I know.
Gaius Fennic, traveller. I was born in Black Marsh of Imperial parents, and I speak a little Jel besides. I've never seen the Empire, so I count myself as from here.
Holds-The-Tally, the guard at the south dock, is about twenty paces south of here. I like him; he's a good sort, and he'll tell you straight.
I'm one of the company's men, posted between the docks and the centre. We stand where the field-owners say, and that's about the size of it.
Cage Door? Easy, stranger. Walk north near sixty paces, and when you come to the dead tree on your right, take the path north-west another fifty or so. Cage Door is right there.
Ha, there you are, my friend! Stand clear of the target line and stay a while. I'm feeling lucky today, and I have thrown well.
Stranger. Mind where you stand, I'm shooting. What d'you want?
Thorn? A fine place to get rich, stranger, if you've got nerve. The hut's about thirty paces west-north-west of here, if it's a bed you're after.
Ask Bites-The-Coin what Thorn is called, stranger. I like her, and I'd bet she tells it better than I would.
Lucan Sevro, archer, hired by the Imperial company. I guard the centre with my bow, and I'm the best shot in Thorn. Ask anyone. Or better, bet on it.
Sheel-Taza is a guard, about ten paces south-west of here. Sour as old milk, so don't expect a smile.
Stay a while, if you like; I've nothing to watch but the crowd, and your company's better.
Traveller. Is there something you need?
Good day, traveller. How can I help you?
If it's your bearings you want, traveller, the signpost is about a dozen paces south-south-east of here. The rest of the town I'm still learning myself.
Ask Holds-The-Tally about the villages around Thorn, traveller. I am still learning who really rules here, and Holds-The-Tally is clever.
I'm Tertius Vallo, a soldier of the hired Imperial company. I stand here and watch the town; that's most of the work.
Gaius Fennic, a soldier of our company, is about twenty paces east-south-east of here. You'll find him there, traveller.
I'm a soldier of the hired company, traveller. Our posts run from the docks up to the signposts at the centre, and mine is just south of them.
Well. You've kept your head down and your hands clean, which is more than most manage. Good to see you, my friend.
I'm on watch, civilian. State your business and keep your voice down.
Yes, civilian? Ask what you need to ask. I'm on duty.
The signposts are about ten paces south-south-west of here, civilian. Read them before you go wandering about.
Ask Decimus Pell why the Owing is defended, civilian. I hold that it is fair, and I keep order on that footing.
Rufio Casca, soldier of the company. I guard the west cages with the Argonian guards, and I say the Owing is fair to anyone who asks.
Wazei-Ru has the cage doors on the west side, about ten paces north-north-east of here. Soft on the prisoners, and I've told Wazei-Ru so.
The company keeps watch on the west cages for the field-owners, civilian. We keep the doors shut and the prisoners where they belong.

Temple Pass, traveller? Follow the path north from here, some hundred and fifty paces, until you reach the stone tower on your left. Then walk north over open ground, some seven hundred paces, and you are there. It is a fair step, so go steady.
Sit a moment if you like. My feet are glad of the excuse.
Traveller. I guard the houses on this side, so keep to the path and we'll have no trouble.
This is the east side, where I stand guard with Jeelus-Vax. There's a house about twenty paces east-north-east of here, if that's the one you want.
Ask Jeelus-Vax about the title, traveller. I think that question is the real fight in Thorn, whatever else you hear.
Severan Otho, soldier of the hired company. Jeelus-Vax and I watch the east houses. It's honest work, traveller, though I'll be glad to go home.
Nalvos Brenur? A Dunmer labourer, held under an Owing, so he works off a debt. He's about twenty paces south of me, and he's a clever one.
Thorn? Follow the path south-west for seventy paces or so; the dead tree will be on your right. From there, south for sixty paces. That is Thorn, party.
For you I have a moment. Speak, and I will hear it.
You are a stranger to me, party. State your business.
Well, party? I have accounts to close. Be brief.
This is Thorn, party. The hut is about forty paces north-north-east of here.
Ask Nalvos Brenur about the ledger, party. I keep it and I collect on it. I am not paid to explain it, party.
I am Quill-Teeth, party, one of the Tax Heel. That is what the people of Thorn call the collectors the field-owners send. I am very good at my work.

Doveth Aralen is a Dunmer held under an Owing, and the eldest of the house's labourers. You will find Doveth about twenty-five paces south-south-east of here. Doveth is slow, party, so ask and then wait.
I collect Owings for the field-owners, party. I also keep the ledger. A person called Owes-Nothing wants it burned, because Owes-Nothing is a debtor in hiding.
The stone tower, party? Climb north-west, about one hundred and forty paces. One hundred and forty. The tower is there.
It is good to see your face again, party. I do not say that to many.
Party. Say what you want, and say it plainly. I see you are armed, so keep your hand away from the blade while you talk.
This is the north side, party, near the houses. A house stands about twenty paces south-east of here.
Ask Mils Ganthis about the charges on an Owing, party. I check every sum I write twice.
Decimus Pell is the one to ask about the Owing, party. I say it is fair because it ends.
I am Tallies-Twice. I collect on the north side for the field-owners, and I face the rising across the north houses. I want it gone from this side.
Breaks-The-Ledger is a soldier of the rising against the Owings. He is about thirty paces west of here, party. Thirty. Keep your weapon near when you go; I say he will strike.
I am a Tax Heel, party. Tolls and Owings on the north side are mine to collect. I check every sum twice. Twice, always.
Stand with us, then. A sharp blade is always welcome here.
Outlander. Say what you want, or leave me.
Why do you interrupt me, outlander? I have work to do.
There is nothing here but open ground, outlander. The house is twenty paces south of here.
Ask Fendyl Omoren about Heita-Meen, outlander. I know the story, and I mean to finish it.
Ask Nalvos Brenur about the families of Thorn, outlander. Mine is a mixed one, and I will say no more of it.
I am Breaks-The-Ledger. I fight for the rising, outlander. That is all you need to know.
Owes-Nothing is a soldier of the rising, like me. You will find him sixty paces south-east of here. He is slower than I would like.
I fight in the rising. We mean to break the Tax Heel's ledgers before anything else. The Tax Heel collect Owings and tolls for the field-owners.
The market's cooking fire? It is north-east of here, a short way. Go on, I have boats to watch.
You are back, my friend. The water is quiet, so stay a while and talk.
Speak. I have boats to watch.
This is Black Rose. The south landing's dock is just south of here. A boat lies just south-south-east. I know her hull.
In the Second Era, word went round the coast that Black Rose had fallen and was gone. It was not. It is still here. I watch its landing.
I am Sakeeth. I watch the south landing for boats that do not pay. I grew up hauling nets on these docks. I joined the guard to be issued boots.
Holds-Fast is the guard on the path above the south docks. He is usually just east-north-east of here. I would trust him in a real fight.
The jail. North-east two hundred and sixty paces. The jail is there.
Haven. South-east a hundred and ten paces, round the cliffs, to the boat on its rack. Then south-west two hundred and thirty paces, past the stone tower. Haven is there.
It is you. Stand by the post a while, my friend. The road is quiet and I am glad of the company.
Stop there. State your business. Let me see what you carry.
The tower is north-north-west of here, about ninety paces. Ahkeeh smokes fish in this town. It is the best thing in Black Rose. I stand at the west gate and count what comes through it.
People say many go into Black Rose and few ever leave. Old prison staff, freed prisoners, deserters and runaways all came here and stayed. I have counted a good many of them through this gate.
The dead lie on the road toward Haven. They are Imperials, with an elf among them. The people of Black Rose have not gone to bury them.
I am Tzeel-Vaa, guard at the west gate. I have stood here longer than the two beside me have been alive. My father guarded this same road for the same pay.
Quintel is the other guard at this gate, grandson of an Imperial jailer. He is usually about five paces north-north-east of me. He is too soft for the work.
The cooking fire by the docks? Walk east about two hundred and twenty-five paces. The fire is there. I charge no toll for directions.
You again. Come, stand a while, my friend. For you there is no fee at this gate. I have said that to very few.
The crossing costs coin. I will name the sum once I have seen your pack.
This is the west gate of Black Rose. I keep the toll here. The marker post is a few paces south-south-west of where you stand. Pass it only once the fee is settled.

Around Black Rose, an owing is taken at a crossing for damage to the way. The debtor works it off on the water. I did that myself once, so I know the sum of it better than most. Now I am the one who takes the toll. I will not apologise for the post.

I am Counts-The-Tolls, guard at this gate. I was a debtor once, working off an owing on the water. I took this post as the way out. I know how that sounds, but the post is paid work and the water was not.

Tzeel-Vaa is the oldest of the three guards at this gate. He is usually about ten paces south-south-east of here. He watches my hands at every cart. He should have retired years ago. Speak to him if you must.
Black Rose Jail, traveller? Walk north-east for some two hundred and fifty paces. The jail is there.
Ah, it is you. Forgive me if I stand stiffly. It is how I was taught. I am glad to see you at the gate again.
Pardon me, traveller. This is the west gate of Black Rose. State your business. I will help if I am able.
This is Black Rose, traveller. The tower stands about ninety paces north-north-west of here.
The people of Black Rose once sent an envoy to the Imperial court. Emperor Pelagius answered him in grunts and squeaks. I do not enjoy telling it, traveller.
I am Quintel, a guard at the west gate. I carry the name of the Imperial jailer who raised my grandmother. I answer to no other. My family has worn a uniform in Black Rose for three generations.
Ahkeeh, the fish smoker, works at the fire west of the gate. You will usually find Ahkeeh about fifty paces north-west of here.
Black Rose Jail. Go north-east for about a hundred and ten paces, until the statue with the sword is on your left. Then north for thirty more. The jail stands there.
I know your step now. Stand with me a while, if you wish.
Speak quietly here. This is a shrine. I do not know you yet.
The standing stone is about ten paces south-south-west of here. Go to it slowly. Do not climb on it.
The first city here belonged to the Lilmothiit, the fox-folk. Every one of them died of a fever, long before Argonians claimed this place.
I guard the standing stone. The other guards did not want the post, so I asked for it. The stone is older than this town. I keep it as a shrine.
Mireel is a guard on the path above the south docks. You will usually find Mireel about seventy paces south-east of here. Do not expect much from the guards at the docks.
The longboat? Go along the boards east for about a hundred and ten paces. The longboat is there. Do you have business aboard?
Sunned and warm? I am glad it is you. I have nothing to report today. Ask me what you like.
Halt. State your business on the boards. I was told to ask every stranger, so I am asking you.
This is the dock walk below the market. I guard it. There is a cooking fire about twenty-five paces south-east of here. The dock is about thirty paces south. Is that what you wanted to know?
When the fever came to Murkmire, the last of the Lilmothiit fled inland toward Black Rose. What became of them is not known. Have you seen any of them on the road?

I am Okaw-Sei, guard of the dock walk. I walk the boards between the dock and the market all day. I was told to watch for anything unusual. I am newly hatched to the guard, but I mean to serve it well.
Teeda-Wan, the guard at the market, is the best fighter on the docks. You will usually find Teeda-Wan about twenty-five paces east-south-east of here.
Walk south about a hundred and thirty paces. The cooking fire is there.
Ah, it is you. I am glad of it. Stand by me a while, the road is quiet.
You again. Good. Stay here with me and ask what you like.
Hm. What do you want? Be quick about it.
Keep to the road, stranger. I am watching it.
This is the road below the jail. There is a house about ten paces south-east of here.
There is a house ten paces south-east of us. I keep watch near it.
Hm. I know little of Black Marsh, but I know the Rose. Its families are three generations deep. A newcomer owes the prison-born for shelter. The ledger is kept by people who were born owing.
The Rose has families three generations deep. If you are new there, you owe the prison-born for your shelter. The ledger is kept by those who were born owing.
Xuth-Ma. I guard the road that runs up to the jail. Most days I talk to Dredges-The-Silt, who stops by the house here.
I am a guard on this road. I do not like the jail. I will not say why.
Dredges-The-Silt keeps the town's channels clear. I know no better company. You will usually find the dredger about five paces north-west of here.
You want Dredges-The-Silt, the dredger who clears the town's channels. Look about five paces north-west of here.
The cooking fire? Walk south about a hundred and twenty paces. It is there. You cannot miss it.
Still watching that jail, as you see. It is good to talk to someone I trust. I am still waiting for the day it is emptied.
What do you want? I am watching the road below the jail. Keep your hands where I can see them.
The house is south-west of here, about twenty paces. Go and look at it yourself.
The families who hold the Rose say it is their home, not a prison. They take it badly when outsiders call it one. I call it a jail. I do not care who hears me.
I am Wazei. I guard this road. My captain has put me where he can see me, because I have been warned twice for wanting a fight with the keepers up there.
Ruh-Jaal is the guard nearest the jail. You will usually find him about thirty-five paces west-north-west of here. Do not expect much of him. He is a coward.
The cooking fire? Walk south about forty-five paces, to the boat on its rack. Then south-west about forty-five more. You will be standing at it. Are you meeting someone there?
Come closer, my friend. Keep your voice down. I hear more on this dock than any other guard. For you I will share it.
Keep your voice low. I do not know your face. I like to know every face on this dock.
You are new here. Who have you been speaking to since you arrived?
Quietly now, though everyone knows it. The dock is about twenty-five paces south-south-west of here. A boat lies about thirty paces the same way.
Quietly now. Ask Quintel about the Imperial court. That is his tale, but I would like to know who else asks him for it.
Ask Tzeel-Vaa about the Haven road. I hear everything said on this dock, not what is said elsewhere. I would like to know what he says.
I am Tuh-Weem. I guard this dock. Everything said on it reaches my ears. I am rarely wrong about what I hear.
Mends-The-Hulls mends boats at the north-east dock. He is usually about fifteen paces north-east of here. I think he is courting someone. Ask him yourself. Tell me what he says.
The longboat? Walk south-east, a hundred and seventy paces or so. The longboat is in front of you.
The water is low this season, so I have time to talk. Stand by me if you like.
Mind where you put your boots. The silt is soft here.
There is a house about ten paces south-east of here. That is all I would point out.
Ask Counts-The-Tolls about crossings and the owing set there. He has forgotten where he came from, so ask him plainly. I have worked mine off in the silt for nine seasons.
I am Dredges-The-Silt. I clear the channels around Black Rose so the boats can pass. It is owing work. It has taken me nine seasons so far.
Xuth-Ma is the guard on the road to the jail. You will usually find him about five paces south-east of here. He is a good man. He is the one who listens to me in the evenings.
The cooking fire? Go south, a hundred and sixty paces or so. The fire is there.
Keep your voice low, and stand by me a while. I will not mind the company.
Move along, if you please. I am on watch.
The standing stone is some forty paces north-west of here. The jail is a little nearer, about thirty-five paces that way. I would not look at it for long.
Ask Wazei about what the families call the Rose. I would rather not say it myself. He is a danger to us all, so keep your voice low when you ask.
I am a guard. I stand nearest the jail and keep my post. That is all there is to say.
Pays-In-Reeds is a reed-weaver. She is kind. You will usually find her about twenty paces north-north-west of here, working off her owing in mats. Ask her, not me.
Black Rose Jail? You can see it from here. It is about sixty paces south-west. Do not wander off the way.
The north district is quiet today. I am glad of it. Stay as long as you like.
Keep to the road and keep your voice down. The families here are asleep or at their work.
This is the north district, where the families live. I know every child in it by name. The house is twenty paces north-north-west of here.
Ask Sakeeth about the Second Era tale that this town was gone. I guard the north district and leave tales to others.
I am Shaleem. I guard the north district, so mind how you behave in it.
Talks-To-Water is a boat captain in the north district. You will usually find him ten paces east-south-east of here. Tell him to take more care with his boat.
The cooking fire? Everyone knows that. Walk south about two hundred and fifteen paces past the house and you will be standing at it. Could you find it without me?
I have been watching the water for boats all day! Do you want to hear what I have noticed?
You are new here, are you not? I notice everyone new. Where did you come from? Did you come by boat?
This is the north district. I know all of it. The house is about fifteen paces east-north-east of here. Why, are you looking for something?
I am Zeeki. I am the cleverest child in the north district. Ask anyone. One day I will captain a boat of my own.
Talks-To-Water, the boat captain? That is the best captain there is. You will usually find the captain about fifteen paces west-south-west of here. Could you ask for a place on the boat for me?
The cooking fire? A sweet first. Go south-east, two hundred and forty paces. The fire is there.
Did you bring a sweet? I have heard things at the jail, and I will tell you them.
Who are you? Stay where I can see you. Have you got a sweet?
The standing stone is five paces south of here. The tower is twenty paces off, north-north-west. Give me a sweet and I will tell you more.
I am Skink. I play by the standing stone, where the other children do not come. I have no family. I hear things at the jail. I tell them for a sweet.
Pays-In-Reeds is nice. She weaves reeds into mats to work off what she owes. She is usually about twenty-five paces east-south-east of here.
The cooking fire by the docks? Listen, water, a stranger wants to walk. Go south-east about seventy paces to the house. Then go south about a hundred and fifty paces. The cooking fire is there.
I told the water you would return. Come, sit by it and tell me what you have seen.
You have the look of someone who does not know the water. What do you want?
Quiet, little ripples, we have a guest. The house is ten paces south-south-east of here. I keep my boat at the north landing.
Long ago the bandit king Red Bramman ruled this country. He raided Topal Bay from here. The First Empire hunted him for years.

Hush, water. You ask for news, stranger. In the Chainbreakers' house, in the north district, Never-Sold has saved coin to buy a woman free of her Owing at the estate north of Blackrose. Never-Sold is asking for a hand with it.
I am Talks-To-Water. I captain a boat out of the north landing. Yes, I talk to the water. My crew is used to it.
Zeeki, the child of the north district, is usually fifteen paces east-north-east of here. That one should be a sailor. I have said so.
The cooking fire? Walk south about eighty paces, until the longboat is on your left. Then the boards, west, about sixty-five paces. The fire is there.
If you have a boat that leaks, bring it to me and I will patch it today.
You are welcome here. Mind the boards, they are wet. What needs mending?
What do you want? I have hulls to patch.
Speak quickly. I am in the middle of a hull.
My house is about ten paces north-east of here. The dock is east-north-east, about twenty-five paces, where the small boats tie up.
North-east, ten paces, is my house. East-north-east, twenty-five paces, is the dock. I patch the boats there.
If you want something to do, Never-Sold needs a hand. The money is ready to buy a woman out of her Owing on the estate north of Blackrose. Ask at the Chainbreakers' house in the north district.
I am Mends-The-Hulls. I patch the small boats at the north-east dock, cheap and fast. My mother taught me the trade. She learned it working off an owing.
I mend hulls. Pitch-Pot says my work is careless, but Pitch-Pot is slow and expensive. My patches hold.
Tuh-Weem is the guard at the north-east boat dock. She is usually about fifteen paces south-west of here. She should mind her own dock.
You want Tuh-Weem, the guard at the north-east boat dock. About fifteen paces south-west of here, as a rule. Go and ask her.
Walk north-west for a little over two hundred paces. You will be at Black Rose Jail. Eat before you go.
There you are, my friend. Sit down and eat. You look thin to me. The pot is hot.
If you want food, say so. If you do not, I have a pot to watch.
This is Black Rose. My cooking fire is ten paces north-west of here. The dock is fifteen or so to the north-north-east. Have you eaten today?
Ask Tzeel-Vaa about who goes into Black Rose and who stays. I came on a prison barge as its cook, and I never got back on it. Have you eaten?
I am Weeska. I cook at the fire and feed the dock hands. Sit, or move along.
Lux Ha mends nets at the market dock, about five paces south-south-west of here. Lux Ha works too hard. I doubt that one has eaten.
The longboat? It is in plain sight. It lies about sixty-three paces east of here. You cannot miss it.
Look at what the boats brought in today. If you have something to sell, I will give you a fair price.
Stranger. Buying or selling? I deal in both.
You want something. Say what it is, or show me what you carry.
The market is where the trade is. The cooking fire is five paces west-north-west of my stall. The dock is ten paces north-north-east.
I am Nuxi-Ra. I sell odds and ends here, whatever the boats bring in. I buy from every crew and I do not ask where a thing came from.
Nuxi-Ra. I trade here at the market.
I buy and I sell. My stall is at the market, by the cooking fire. My stock is whatever the boats bring in. Show me what you have and I will name a price.
Rows-Against-It captains a boat from the market dock, and is usually about twenty-five paces south-south-west of here. Of all the captains, that is the one who pays on time.
Walk along the boards north-east, ninety paces or so. The longboat is there. You cannot miss it.
Calm water today, and a fare I know. My boat is yours if you need her.
You want a crossing, say where. If not, I have rope to mend.
My boat is ten paces south of here. The dock is five paces south-east, so mind your feet on the boards.
Ask Okaw-Sei about the last of the Lilmothiit. I carry fares, not old stories. If you want a crossing, say where.
I am Rows-Against-It. I run this boat from the market dock to wherever a fare will go. I paid off my owing on the water and kept the boat. No crossing-keeper gives me orders now.
Weeska cooks at the market fire. She is usually about twenty paces north-east of here.
The jail. North, two hundred and thirty paces. Black Rose Jail is there.
You again, my friend. Good. Stand by the fire and watch the market with me.
Show me your hands. Then say what you want.
Yes. What do you want?
This is the market. The cooking fire is five paces south of here. The dock is fifteen paces south. Keep the peace and you will have no trouble from me.
Ask Xuth-Ma about the families of the Rose. He talks of it. I do not.
Teeda-Wan. I keep the peace at this market. That is all.
Lux Ha works the nets on the market dock. About ten paces east-south-east of here, usually. Lux Ha should be paid more.
The longboat. Yes. Walk south-east, about a hundred and fifty-five paces, until the house is on your left. Then walk south, about a hundred paces more. The longboat is there.
Hm. Stand with me a while. I am in no hurry. I am glad it is you.
You wish to speak with me? Then speak. I am Iron-Jaw. I guard the north district.
Hm. There is the house, just there, about ten paces north-north-west of where we stand.
Hm. Ask Quintel about Emperor Pelagius. I would like to read his tale in a book one day.
I am Iron-Jaw. A cudgel struck my face in my first year. The name stayed with me. I have stood in the north district ever since. I can read well.
Shaleem is the person you want. Shaleem is a guard in the north district. She is the best guard in the town. You will usually find Shaleem about five paces south-south-east of here.
The cooking fire? Go south past Black Rose, about three hundred and thirty-five paces. The cooking fire is there.
Come and stand with me by the boats a while. I could use the company.
I do not know you. Why are you at the landing?
You are a stranger here. Keep clear of the boats.
There is a boat about twenty paces north-north-west of here. A rowing boat lies thirty-five paces north.
Black Rose and Lilmoth have been rivals for as long as anyone has kept count. I am a guard, not a teller of old tales.
I am Raxa-Tum. I guard the north landing, where the fishing boats tie up. I was a fisher myself once.
Okeemu is the best fisher in town. You will usually find Okeemu about twenty-five paces south-west of here, at the north landing.
The jail. Walk south-west about one hundred and seventy-five paces. Black Rose Jail is there.
You have come up the road again, my friend. I keep the road, as ever. Speak if you wish.
State your business on the north road.
Halt. Say what you want. I am on watch.
This is the north road into Black Rose. The northern marker post is about fifteen paces south of here. A boat lies about thirty-five paces east-south-east.
I keep watch here, above the northern marker post. The post is about fifteen paces south. There is a boat about thirty-five paces east-south-east of where we stand.

In Empress Morihatha's day the people of Black Rose raised an army against the Empire. Her battlemage Welloc broke it with a spell, not with soldiers. No one in the town has trusted a battlemage since.
I am Watches-The-Road. I guard the north road into town. I report every lapse I see. That includes the lapses of other guards.
I am a guard. I watch the north road and I report what I find.
Raxa-Tum, the guard at the north landing, is usually about fifty paces north-north-west of here. He fishes on duty. He should be dismissed.
The cooking fire? Walk south past the house, about three hundred paces. You will find it there.
The water is good today. Sit by me a while.
I am fishing, so please speak softly.
This is the north landing of Black Rose. My boat is there, forty paces to the north-north-east.
Ask Keeps-The-Stone about the Lilmothiit. I know the water and the fish. That is enough for me.
I am Okeemu. I fish from the north landing with my family. My boat is the oldest at the landing.
Heshra, the fishwife at the north landing, is usually about five paces west of here.

Walk south-east about sixty-five paces. Black Rose will be on your left. Then south about eighty paces, until the statue is on your left. Then south-east about sixty-five paces, until the house is on your left. Then south about ninety paces. The longboat is there.
For you I will not haggle. Come closer and look at the catch.
What do you want? If you are buying, say what you want and what you will pay.
This is the north landing, where I gut and sell the catch. The house is about forty paces south-south-west of here.
I am Heshra. I gut and sell Okeemu's catch here. I run my family. I watch the prices. A buyer does not bargain with me twice.
Okeemu is usually about five paces east of here. Okeemu is too soft to ask what a catch is worth, so I do the selling.
The cooking fire is south of here. Walk past the house, about three hundred paces. You will find it.
It is you, my friend. I practised with my stick today. Nobody laughed.
Oh. Hello. I am helping with the nets, so I cannot talk for long.
I do not know you. What do you want?
The boat is just there, a little east of north. It is only thirty-odd paces from here.
I am Pip. Okeemu and Heshra are my parents. I help them with the nets. I am going to be a guard. I practise with this stick.
Raxa-Tum is the guard at the north landing. You will usually find Raxa-Tum about twenty-five paces north-east of here. Raxa-Tum is the best guard.
Walk north, two hundred paces or near it. Black Rose Jail is there.
You again, my friend. Good. The path is quiet, so stay a while.
Keep your hand clear of your weapon. Then say what you want.
The dock is twenty-five paces east-south-east. Thirty paces south-east, you will see a rowing boat.
Ask Watches-The-Road about the old rising against the Empire. I guard a path. I do not tell tales.
They call me Holds-Fast. I was the last one standing in a brawl on the docks. The name stayed. I guard the south path. I would rather be feared than liked.
Ten-Coins guards between the south docks and the market. He is usually twenty-five paces north-north-east of here. He will hang one day.
The cooking fire? It is in plain sight, about seventy paces east. Walk straight towards it.
At last I know your name. Stand easy. I do not say that to many.
I do not know you. State your name and your business. Spell the name if it is unusual.
This is Black Rose. The dock is about thirty-five paces south-east of here.
Ask Raxa-Tum about Black Rose and Lilmoth. I know Lilmoth. It is a midden.
I am Mireel. I came to Black Rose from Lilmoth and stayed. The guard took me because I can read. I keep the duty rolls for the south docks.
Holds-Fast is usually about fifteen paces south-south-east of here, on this same path. He is a brute, but a useful one.
Walk north about a hundred and seventy paces. You are at Black Rose Jail. I give this way free.
Ah, there you are. Stand with me a while. Today I will name you no price.
Keep your purse close, stranger. Then we will get on well.
You want something from me? Most things here have a price. Mine is always fair.
This is Black Rose. The house is about thirty-five paces north-east of here. The market's cooking fire is about forty paces east.
Ask Xuth-Ma about the Rose and its families. He gives that away for nothing. I give nothing away.
I am Ten-Coins. The name is the price of looking away. Everyone at the docks knows it. I call it a fee, and I call it a fair one.
Okaw-Sei is a guard like me, on the dock walk below the market. You will usually find him about fifteen paces east-south-east of here.
The cooking fire is in plain sight, about forty-five paces south-south-west of here. Walk straight to it.
The dock is quiet. You may stand with me, if you wish.
This dock is watched. Say who you are and why you are here.
I stand on the east dock of Black Rose. There is a house ten paces north-west of me, and a boat fifteen paces south-east. I keep watch between them.
Ask Watches-The-Road about the town's old war with the Empire. A deserter taught me the sword, not the town's history.
I am Corvane, guard of the east dock and of the big ship moored past it. I took my name from a deserter who taught me the sword. We came to Black Rose together. I stayed after he left.
Pitch-Pot seals the boats at this dock. He works harder than anyone on the docks. You will usually find him about five paces east-south-east of me.
The jail? Walk north-west, about a hundred and ninety paces. Black Rose Jail is there.
I smell of pitch, I know, but I am glad to see you! Come close.
Mind your feet. The pitch is hot. You will smell me before you see me.
Stand back from the pot or you will be burned. What do you want?
I seal hulls here, so I can tell you about boats. The big ship is about forty paces east-south-east of here. A boat lies about twenty paces south-east.
Ask Sakeeth about the old talk that Black Rose had fallen! I know tar, leaks and rot. She knows the rest.
They call me Pitch-Pot. I got the name as a hatchling, when I fell into the pot. I have smelled of tar ever since.
Corvane is the guard on the east dock. He is a good sort. He is usually a few paces west-north-west of here.
The cooking fire? Go south, a hundred and eighty paces or so. The fire is there.
The next mat can wait. Sit by me a while.
Mind the reed. I am counting mats.
My house is north of here, about fifteen paces. It is the one by the road.
Ask Counts-The-Tolls about the crossing and its owings. I pay mine in mats. It is the ledger I mind, not the work.

Never-Sold has put money aside to buy a woman out of her Owing on the estate north of Blackrose. He is looking for someone to lend a hand. I know what an Owing weighs. Look for Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house, in the north district.
I am Pays-In-Reeds. I weave mats and baskets from marsh reed. I make one mat a day, and that pays my owing. I am working toward my last mat.
Skink is the child who plays by the jail's standing stone, about twenty-five paces west-north-west of here. That child should be in a home, not out by a jail.
Walk north-west, about two hundred and twenty paces. Black Rose Jail is there.
My hands will keep working, but I am glad of the company. Sit a while.
Yes? Mind the net, please. I am in the middle of a knot.
This is Black Rose, the market dock. The cooking fire is about ten paces west-south-west of here. A boat lies about twenty-five paces south-south-west.
Ask Raxa-Tum about Lilmoth. I was born here and have never left, so I can tell you nothing of it.
I am Lux Ha. I mend the nets that come off the market boats. There is always more to mend. I was born in Black Rose and have never left it.
You will usually find Nuxi-Ra, the street vendor at the market, about ten paces north of here.
Walk south-west about a hundred and fifteen paces, to the longboat on your left. Then west along the boards, sixty-five paces. The cooking fire is there.
Few people come out this far. You are always welcome, my friend. Sit by the water.
Yes? Say what you want.
You are on my dock. Speak, then.
The dock is a few paces south-east of here. My house is ten paces north.
Ask Keeps-The-Stone about the fox-folk. It is not mine to tell. I live at the edge for the quiet.
There is smoke from the stone house just west of my dock. People are shut inside it, and Third-Born Tsaxi keeps the door.
I am Ree-Shaal. I fish from this dock and live in the house behind it.
I moved out to the edge to be away from the town. I like the quiet. Visitors spoil it.
Sleeps-Standing, the guard at the far east dock, is usually about twenty paces south-east of here. Go and talk to him.
The cooking fire? Climb west, a hundred and thirty-five paces or so, until the longboat is on your left. Then take the boards west, sixty-five paces more. The cooking fire is there.
Hnn. Come, stand with me. Nothing is happening here, and I like it better with you.
Hnn. Yes? Speak. I am listening.
Hm. What is it? Say it plainly.
The dock is there, about five paces east-south-east. The house is ten paces west-south-west. There is not much else to see. I prefer it that way.
Ask Talks-To-Water about Red Bramman. I only stand a post, and I would sooner sleep.
Hnn. Smoke rises from the stone house west-north-west of here. Third-Born Tsaxi stands at its door. People are shut in there.
I am Sleeps-Standing. I guard the dock at the eastern edge of Black Rose, where nothing happens. I have learned to sleep on my feet. I wake quickly when I must.
Ree-Shaal, the fisher at the far east dock? Usually about twenty paces north-west of here. Ree-Shaal is a sour one. Ree-Shaal complains about me. Hnn.
Go west along the boards, about a hundred paces, past the longboat. The cooking fire is there.
You are a welcome sight after a day of crates. Sit a moment, if you can.
Yes. What do you want?
The big ship is some twenty paces west of here. My house is a few paces north-east, beside it.
Ask Tzeel-Vaa about those who come to Black Rose and stay. I came on a ship myself. I have not decided yet if I was wise to stay.
I am Ojeel. I unload the big ship whenever it comes in. I live in the house by its berth. I signed on to a crew once and walked off it here.
Tadpole, the child who plays around the big ships, is usually about forty paces south of here. That child should be kept off the ships.
The cooking fire? Go along the boards north-west, only about a hundred and ten paces past the longboat. You will be at the fire. It is easy.
Did you see the ship? Is it still there? I kept watch while you were gone.
Who are you? Are you here to see the ships? Did you drop a coin? I will look for it if you did.
This is the east docks. Can you not see the big ship? It is just there, twenty paces west-north-west. The dock is ten paces north-west. I know every board of it.
I am Tadpole. I play between the big ships and run errands for the crews. One day I will sail on one. Then you will hear of me. What is your name?
Ojeel? He unloads the big ship. He is always about forty paces north of here. He chases me off the ship every time. Why do you want him?
Haven? Walk south-east about two hundred and fifty paces, until you reach the stone tower. Then south-west a little over a hundred and thirty paces. Haven is there.
The cooking fire? Walk east about two hundred and eighty paces. You will find it there.
The next fish will not be long, so sit by the fire.
Come near the fire and tell me what you need.
The fish is still on the fire. Say what you want.
You are standing in my smoke. Speak, or buy something.
My cooking fire is about twenty paces west-south-west of here, outside the west gate. The tower is forty paces north.
Ask Talks-To-Water about the old bandit king. I know fish and smoke. That tale takes longer than a fish.
For news of the road toward Haven, ask Tzeel-Vaa. He is the only honest guard at the west gate, so he will tell it straight.

I am Ahkeeh. I smoke fish over this fire outside the west gate. I sell it to the guards and to anyone coming in by road. I was born on a boat and came ashore when it sank. I have not been on the water since.
Tzeel-Vaa is the oldest of the three guards at the west gate. He is the only honest one. Look about fifty-five paces south-east of here. That is where Tzeel-Vaa usually stands.
Ask Gih-Xaleel about the alleys, and wipe your feet before you come in. I keep this floor clean.
You again. Come in out of the wet, friend. Mind the floor, though.
You. State your business, or move on.
This is the hall. The iron door opens on the street by the gate, thirty paces north-north-west of the warden. Stay inside if you have sense.
Helstrom has a name for being dangerous. The city has never been taken. I have heard worse tales than that.
Ask Namorine about Stormhold. I say the Stormhold folk are soft. I say it to anyone who asks.
Levy soldier. I guard this hall. I would sooner be indoors than on the street.
Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden. He keeps the gate, just outside that door. Go and see him.
